guides.title: Controlled server DataTable
guides.summary: Render a server page with typed columns, stable selection and native keyboard controls.
guides.markdown:
Import DataTable, DataTableProps<Row>, DataTableColumn<Row> and DataTableState from the public UI package. Compose with component(DataTable<Row>, props). Columns use either a key from the row type or an accessor function. An optional cell callback receives the typed row and returns a renderer value. Without a cell callback, values render as escaped text.

Provide rows for the current page, rowCount for all matching records, and a one-based state containing page, pageSize, filter and optional sort. The table does not fetch, sort, filter or slice data. onStateChange receives a new query state. Filtering, sorting and page-size changes reset page to 1. The parent must fetch that state and prevent stale responses from replacing newer results. Reconcile a page beyond the updated total in the parent. The Previous page control can recover to the new last page.

getRowId must return a stable, nonempty string. Duplicate row and column IDs are rejected. Never derive an ID from the page index. For selection, provide both selection and onSelectionChange. The callback receives a fresh Set. Select-visible affects only selectable rows on this page and preserves off-page IDs. Filtering preserves IDs too. Clear or reconcile selection in the parent when your application policy requires it. Always authorize selected IDs on the server before an action.

Use loading while a query is pending, error for a safe user-facing failure message, and onRetry for retry behavior. Stale rows can remain visible while loading, but selection is blocked. Empty results and an empty out-of-range page have separate status text. The table forwards no arbitrary HTML attributes. Use its declared props rather than relying on an untyped attribute spread.

A visible caption is required. Give each table a unique id when query changes use same-page navigation. It supplies stable IDs for the filter, page-size, sort and paging controls so Cossack can restore focus after replacing the page. Native table headers, buttons, search input, select and checkboxes provide semantics and keyboard behavior. rowLabel names each selection checkbox and defaults to its ID. Sort headers expose aria-sort. The page-selection checkbox reports a mixed state. Paging buttons remain focusable with aria-disabled and ignore inactive actions, preserving focus during loading and at page boundaries. Retry moves focus to the filter before invoking the callback. Loading and result counts use a polite status region; errors use an alert. Load the UI theme as for other UI components.

The public-type, SSR and Chromium HTTP-data tests cover this contract. Generated Node and local workerd applications exercise server resources, URL queries, selection and hydration. The full runtime matrix and broader UI accessibility audit remain separate acceptance work.

guides.title: Typed native controls
guides.summary: Use typed native attributes, @event listeners and accessible labels with buttons, inputs, textarea, selects, choice controls and forms.
guides.markdown:
Button, Input, Label, Checkbox, Switch and Form declare native attributes without an arbitrary string/any index signature. component() checks the component's own props. Pass children as its third argument. Use lower-case HTML attribute names, such as tabindex and readonly. Native disabled/required values are booleans, not strings or loading counts. Use !!loading or loading > 0. Visual size is default, sm or lg; it is not the numeric HTML input size. data-* accepts scalar values. ARIA attributes use DOM-defined names and serialize booleans/numbers as text.

Use @click, @input, @change and other DOM event names. React-style onClick is not a listener. NativeEvents<Element> gives each listener the DOM event type and the exact control as currentTarget. target can be a descendant. Capture currentTarget before awaiting; native events clear currentTarget after dispatch. Form's submit callback has an HTMLFormElement currentTarget and prevents native navigation. It defaults to novalidate; set novalidate:false to keep browser constraint validation. Omit submit for a native form submission. Choose Button type explicitly inside forms: button for actions, submit for submission, reset for native reset behavior. A missing type retains the browser's submit default.

Input's value attribute supplies native default markup. Use .value for reactive values, bind() for two-way binding or live() for explicit DOM reconciliation. The .checked and .indeterminate properties are also available on Input. Checkbox and Switch instead own checked through their checked prop; use @change and event.currentTarget.checked to update parent state. Do not override their type, role or checked property through a competing spread. Checkbox supports indeterminate and label; label takes precedence over children. Switch children supply visible label content. Native form names and values are forwarded to the input, so unchecked/disabled controls follow normal FormData rules.

Give Input a visible Label with matching for/id, or an aria-label. Checkbox and Switch need label content or aria-label. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. Link field help/errors with aria-describedby and publish validation state with aria-invalid. Labels, keyboard behavior and native disabled/required validation remain browser-owned. class merges with the component's base classes; id, names, ARIA, data attributes and listeners target the native control, not the Checkbox/Switch label wrapper.

Published declaration tests reject misspelled props/events, invalid values and competing control ownership. Chromium covers labels, keyboard toggles, parent-controlled reset, native validation, event targets and FormData. Other UI components still have separate contract/accessibility audit work; this guide does not assert coverage for the entire catalog.

Textarea, Select and NativeSelect also declare native props and exact event currentTarget types. Give each control a visible Label with matching for/id and use aria-describedby for help/errors. Both select components use native browser selection and keyboard behavior. Use .value (plain, bind() or live()) for text or selection. Their types reject a value attribute because native textarea/select HTML does not initialize values from that attribute. SSR places textarea values in escaped text and selects the matching option, including nested/dynamic options. Hydration retains the native controls. Null/undefined property values serialize as empty text. A leading textarea newline is preserved. Pass selected options as children for multiple selections; a scalar .value selects only the first matching option, even with multiple:true. For a single select, supply an option matching its SSR value: HTML without a selected option defaults to the first available option, so an unmatched value cannot represent selectedIndex=-1 before JavaScript runs. Plain select values preserve manual choices on unrelated renders; live() reapplies the requested value after dynamic options commit. Textarea content must use .value rather than interpolated child text, since raw-text HTML cannot carry renderer comment anchors.

InputGroup forwards native input attributes and event targets to its input; prefix and suffix are rendered as adornments. They do not replace an accessible label. Use matching Label for/id and connect units, help and errors through aria-describedby. Its wrapper error style follows the input aria-invalid state. Native disabled affects the input; authors own the disabled state of interactive addon content.

PasswordInput owns type, value and disabled across its native field and reveal button. Use value with onChange(value, event) for parent state. Unchanged values preserve native edits on reveal. onChange runs before a supplied @input listener; both receive the same native input currentTarget, and preventDefault directives retain their validation option. Other native listeners also target the input. Use autocomplete:new-password for creation forms; current-password is the default. Empty placeholders stay empty. Localize showLabel and hideLabel for the reveal button. Give each password field a label and unique id; the toggle references that id through aria-controls. Pointer reveal preserves input focus and selection. Keyboard reveal keeps the button focused for repeated operation. Disabled fields and inherited disabled fieldsets block reveal. Do not pass type, .value or ?disabled to override component-owned state; use disabled instead.

ARIA relationship attributes (aria-controls, aria-describedby, aria-labelledby, aria-activedescendant, aria-details, aria-errormessage, aria-flowto and aria-owns) accept string IDs, not DOM elements. Element/Elements reflection property names are not HTML attribute names.

guides.title: Radio groups and numeric sliders
guides.summary: Keep native choice, range, form, event and accessibility behavior explicit.
guides.markdown:
RadioGroup renders a div with role=radiogroup and native radio inputs. Give each logical group a distinct nonempty name within its form, unique string item values, and an accessible group name through aria-label or aria-labelledby. Item labels fall back to their values. Optional item IDs must be unique in the document. Items are keyed by value so reordering retains their DOM identity. value identifies the current selection. Update it in onValueChange(value, event); event.currentTarget is the input. Native @change still bubbles to the root div, so that listener's currentTarget is HTMLDivElement and target is the input. Capture a native event's currentTarget before awaiting.

RadioGroup disabled, required and form apply to every input. Item disabled adds a per-choice restriction. Browser radio grouping, arrow keys and form validation remain native. orientation controls layout and aria-orientation. Other declared global attributes/events target the div, not each input. Text-input attributes and competing role/orientation overrides are rejected by types. Duplicate values and an empty name fail explicitly.

Slider renders a native range input. value, min, max and step are finite numbers; max must be at least min and step must be positive. The browser clamps the requested value and applies step. The component sets constraints before the controlled value and reconciles that value when bounds change, including when a previously clamped value becomes valid. Handle @input on the native input and read event.currentTarget.valueAsNumber to update parent state. Use Input with type=range if you need a direct native wrapper instead of this controlled Slider contract.

Give Slider a visible external Label using for/id, label, aria-label or aria-labelledby. label takes precedence over aria-label without emitting duplicate attributes. name, form and list target the input. The range type, numeric state and implicit value semantics remain component-owned; text-input attributes and competing .value bindings are rejected. Disabled appearance follows native :disabled state, including inherited fieldsets.

Checkbox, Switch and RadioGroup labels style themselves from their child input's actual disabled state. This also handles inherited disabled fieldsets. Chromium acceptance builds the real Tailwind/UI theme and verifies light/dark disabled appearance, native keyboard behavior, a Switch focus ring, callback targets, parent radio resets, keyed identity and range bounds. This does not close the full UI catalog or runtime matrix.

guides.title: Native one-time-code input
guides.summary: Use one accessible input with decorative digit slots and explicit controlled state.
guides.markdown:
Compose InputOTP with length (an integer from 1 to 32, default 6), name and a label through id/for or aria-label. One native text input owns form submission, selection, keyboard editing and autocomplete=one-time-code. Decorative digit slots are hidden from assistive technology. Only ASCII digits remain in the code. Leading zeroes are preserved.

Use defaultValue for an uncontrolled initial code. Use value with onChange to control the code. The parent must accept the proposed value to retain an edit. Parent value changes update the input and slots. onChange(code, event) runs when a user edit changes the normalized code. onComplete(code, event) follows for a complete code. Initial and parent values do not emit these callbacks. Completion reports a proposed code, not acceptance or verification by a server.

Native attributes and @events target the input. The component owns type, inputmode, maxlength, minlength, pattern and .value. Paste replaces the current selection and removes separators. A native @paste listener can prevent the operation. Composition text remains intact until composition ends. required uses native validation. disabled, readonly and inherited disabled fieldsets retain native behavior.

Form reset restores the initial uncontrolled code or current controlled value without emitting change/completion callbacks. A canceled reset keeps the current code. Treat the code as text, never a number. Verify it on the server using the application's expiration and attempt rules.

guides.title: Restricted-choice Combobox
guides.summary: Keep a typed selected option separate from editable search text and native form values.
guides.markdown:
Compose Combobox with a stable, page-unique id and options containing unique nonempty string values and nonempty labels. Add a label whose for matches id, or supply aria-label. Native attributes and @events target the visible text input. The component owns its role, popup ARIA relationships, autocomplete and value. name and form also target a hidden input that submits the selected option value, never a label or search text. Input IDs determine stable listbox and option IDs during SSR and hydration.

Use defaultValue for an uncontrolled initial selection. Use value and onChange to control selection; the parent must accept the proposed value to retain it. Missing or disabled selected options display and submit an empty value. Parent value changes cancel an old search. Typing filters labels but never commits arbitrary text. Select an enabled option with the pointer or Arrow keys and Enter. Escape, Tab, blur and light dismissal close the popup and restore the committed label. The text input retains focus while aria-activedescendant identifies the active option. Native text editing keys remain available. Native @keydown can cancel the internal action.

Options with disabled=true cannot be chosen. disabled, readonly and enclosing disabled fieldsets prevent editing. Required fields need a selected option; search text alone does not satisfy validation. Localize placeholder, emptyLabel and requiredMessage. Form reset restores the initial uncontrolled selection or current controlled value without calling onChange. Canceled resets preserve selection. This component requires JavaScript for option selection; SSR supplies the initial label, field value and ARIA structure.

Keyboard behavior follows the editable restricted-choice pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/. Browser fixtures prove the implemented keyboard, focus and form behavior; full assistive-technology and runtime release acceptance remains separate.

guides.title: MultiSelect tags and form values
guides.summary: Select or create tags with typed native input props, visible validation and repeated form submission.
guides.markdown:
Compose MultiSelect with a stable page-unique id and a label through for=id or aria-label. options and selected values contain unique nonempty strings. Native attributes and @events target the editable input. The component owns its role, popup ARIA relationships, input value and validation attributes. name creates one hidden input per selected value. Read submitted selections with FormData.getAll(name). form associates the editable input and every hidden value with an external form.

Use defaultValue for an uncontrolled initial array. Use value with onChange to control selection; accept the fresh array to retain an edit. The component never mutates supplied arrays. Parent selection changes cancel stale searches. Existing parent values remain visible even if options change. allowCreate=false restricts new additions, not parent-owned values. New custom values are trimmed. Duplicate custom labels are matched without case differences. max is a nonnegative integer; zero means unlimited. Existing over-limit selections are preserved and invalid, rather than silently truncated.

Typing filters unselected options. Arrow keys highlight suggestions, Enter adds the highlighted option or an exact match/custom candidate, and Escape or Tab dismisses search. Composition Enter does not add a tag. Backspace with an empty query removes the last tag. Remove buttons have localizable labels and preserve keyboard focus among remaining chips; pointer removal returns focus to the input. Native @keydown can veto internal actions. The popup describes one proposed addition, not a second list of the full selection.

validate checks every proposed addition, including predefined options. Return a string to show a role=alert message and block form submission, or null to accept. error supplies a parent-owned message that stays until the parent clears it. aria-describedby retains caller-provided descriptions and adds the error ID. Required validation depends on selected tags, not search text. Localize placeholder, emptyLabel, requiredMessage, maxMessage, createLabel and removeLabel. Escape/blur dismiss an attempted-add error; they do not clear a parent error.

disabled and inherited disabled fieldsets block additions/removal and exclude hidden values from submission. readonly blocks edits but retains submitted values. Form reset restores the initial uncontrolled array or current controlled array without calling onChange; canceled resets preserve selection. SSR renders the initial tags and form values; JavaScript is required to edit tags. Browser acceptance covers native forms, keyboard/focus and popup behavior. Full application and assistive-technology acceptance remains part of the release audit.

guides.title: Calendar and native DatePicker
guides.summary: Use strict Gregorian date strings, bounded keyboard navigation and native form validation.
guides.markdown:
Calendar and DatePicker require stable page-unique id props. Dates are Gregorian yyyy-mm-dd strings from year 0001 through 9999; an empty value means no selection. Invalid dates such as February 30 and inverted min/max bounds throw clear errors. isCalendarDate(value) tests external data without throwing and returns false for empty values or timestamps. Preserve invalid database text in a text editor rather than silently rolling it into another day.

Use value with onChange for controlled state; accept proposed changes to retain them. defaultValue initializes uncontrolled state. Initial and parent updates do not call onChange. Calendar onSelect runs for every accepted user pick, including the already selected date. Calendar native attributes and @events target its root div. DatePicker native attributes and @events target its date input. The components own their roles and values.

Calendar renders the selected month before JavaScript runs. It uses a named grid, full weekday/date labels, a live month heading and one day in the tab sequence. Arrows navigate days/weeks; Home/End move within the configured week; PageUp/PageDown move months, with Shift for years. Navigation clamps at min/max and month ends, including leap days. Enter or Space picks the active day. Rapid keys use the latest navigation state. readonly permits Calendar navigation but blocks selection; disabled blocks all controls.

DatePicker uses an input of type=date for native editing, required/min/max validation, name/form submission and reset. A separate labeled button opens the shared Calendar in a nonmodal popover. Opening focuses the selected or bounded reference day. Selection and Escape return trigger focus; Tab can leave and close the panel. Clicking outside dismisses without stealing focus. Readonly and disabled fields block the custom picker, including inherited disabled fieldsets. Choosing a calendar date dispatches input on the native field. High-level onChange also covers native edits and clearing. The native browser date picker remains available; there is no placeholder contract.

The custom calendar uses locale (default en-US), weekStartsOn (Sunday=0 through Saturday=6), previousLabel and nextLabel. DatePicker also has openLabel and calendarLabel. Its native input display follows browser settings. Arithmetic and formatting use UTC to avoid host timezone/DST drift. Pass today as the application's desired date for deterministic SSR and a local-day marker; its default is the current UTC day. This is date-only handling, not timestamp conversion.

Native/canceled reset restores or preserves initial uncontrolled values or current controlled values without callbacks. Out-of-range but real parent dates remain visible in DatePicker and fail native validation; the popup focuses a date within range. Browser fixtures cover keyboard/focus, hydration, date limits and native forms. Full assistive-technology and release-runtime acceptance remains separate.

guides.title: Native Modal, Sheet and Drawer
guides.summary: Control native modal state, dismissal, accessible names and dialog events.
guides.markdown:
Modal, Sheet and Drawer use the native dialog element. Pass an accessible name through aria-label or aria-labelledby. Drawer title supplies a visible heading and fallback name. Native attributes and @event callbacks target the dialog, including Drawer. Events expose HTMLDialogElement as currentTarget. The component owns open, role, aria-modal and tabindex. Arbitrary props and .open are rejected by public types.

Use open for controlled state. onClose reports user or native dismissal, including Escape, backdrop clicks, Drawer close and method=dialog forms. Accept dismissal by setting open=false. If open remains true, the dialog reopens. Prop-driven closing and cleanup do not call onClose. @close observes native close events, including prop-driven closing. Native events run once with the actual dialog as currentTarget. Prevent default on @cancel to veto Escape. closeOnEscape=false also vetoes Escape. closeOnBackdrop=false disables backdrop dismissal. Backdrop dismissal requires a pointer press and click outside the panel. Keyboard/programmatic clicks do not dismiss.

For uncontrolled state, use defaultOpen. It applies once, and unrelated renders do not reopen a dismissed dialog. Server-rendered dialogs remain closed, including open=true and defaultOpen=true. After connection, showModal opens them. Supply another route or visible content when essential information must work without JavaScript.

The browser provides autofocus, inert background content, native form validation and focus restoration. Place autofocus on the appropriate child. Native keyboard navigation can reach browser chrome. Do not add a custom focus trap. A method=dialog form closes only after native validation succeeds. Read its returnValue from onClose. Reopening clears the previous returnValue. Cleanup closes the dialog and releases its native modal state.

Sheet and Drawer side selects left, right, top or bottom. Their size is a CSS width or height. Modal size is a maximum-width utility class. Sheet fullScreen expands the panel to the viewport. Drawer closeLabel localizes its close button, which is available on all sides unless showCloseButton=false. Load the UI theme for panel and backdrop styling. Native dialog attributes, including style and class, apply to the dialog container rather than its panel.

Public declaration, SSR and themed Chromium tests cover these contracts. Other browser engines, assistive technologies, Popover and the full release matrix remain separate acceptance work.

guides.title: Native nonmodal Popover
guides.summary: Use stable IDs, typed trigger and panel attributes, native dismissal and bounded positioning.
guides.markdown:
Import Popover, PopoverProps and PopoverContentProps from the public UI package. Provide a page-unique, nonempty id without whitespace. It identifies the native trigger button. The panel ID is id followed by -content. Stable IDs keep native targeting intact through SSR and hydration. Pass trigger as noninteractive button content and children as the third component() argument. Give the trigger a visible name or aria-label.

Top-level native attributes and @event listeners target HTMLButtonElement. contentProps supplies attributes and listeners for HTMLDivElement. IDs, trigger type, popovertarget, popovertargetaction and expansion semantics belong to the component or browser. Unknown props are rejected. Do not pass open: this component uses native auto-popover state. Use its show(), hide() and toggle() methods when imperative control is needed. Calls before connection or after cleanup do nothing. A disabled trigger, including an inherited disabled fieldset, cannot open the panel and closes an existing panel.

Native popovertarget supplies the accessibility relationship and expanded state. The panel has no automatic dialog or menu role. Choose contentProps.role and an appropriate accessible name for interactive panels. If you choose menu semantics, provide the menu keyboard behavior too; Popover supplies no menu navigation. It is nonmodal and does not trap focus. Without autofocus on a descendant, opening retains trigger focus. Tab enters the content in native order. Escape and outside clicks use native dismissal. Focus restoration follows the browser, so outside clicks retain their new focus target. Native targeting and dismissal still work without JavaScript; custom positioning requires hydration.

Top-level @click can prevent trigger activation. contentProps['@beforetoggle'] can prevent opening. Closing is not cancelable through beforetoggle. contentProps['@toggle'] observes native state changes with the real panel as currentTarget. Native toggle events can coalesce rapid changes. Supplied callbacks and preventDefault directives retain native behavior while internal positioning remains active. Keep callbacks synchronous when vetoing default behavior.

side chooses top, bottom, left or right, with top as the default. align chooses start, center or end, with center as the default. Horizontal start/end follows the trigger's direction. The panel flips to the opposite side when that side has more space, then clamps to the visual viewport with an eight-pixel gap. data-side reports the actual side. Nested scrolling, viewport changes and trigger/content size changes update positioning. Oversized content scrolls inside viewport limits. contentProps.style can set width or height; the component owns position, inset, top, left, margin, box-sizing, overflow, max-width and max-height. Load the UI theme for styling. Cleanup removes listeners and observers and closes the panel.

Public declarations, deterministic SSR and themed Chromium tests cover the contract. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the broader release matrix remain separate acceptance work.

guides.title: Dropdown and context action menus
guides.summary: Author named single-level menus with typed actions, keyboard navigation and focus restoration.
guides.markdown:
Import DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, MenuItem and MenuPanelProps from the public UI package. Both menus require a stable, page-unique id without whitespace. The panel ID is id followed by -menu. DropdownMenu uses a native trigger button. Its top-level attributes and @event listeners target HTMLButtonElement. ContextMenu wraps the context region in a focusable div. Its top-level attributes and events target HTMLDivElement. ContextMenu also requires menuLabel to name the menu. Give the context region its own label when needed. menuProps targets the menu div. IDs, menu roles, native targeting and expansion semantics are owned by the components.

Use readonly MenuItem arrays for actions. An action requires a nonempty string label and accepts onClick, disabled and destructive. onClick receives the native button event with HTMLButtonElement as currentTarget. Separators are separate {separator:true} entries and cannot also be actions. ContextMenu previously treated separator as a divider before a possible action; split such entries into a separator and an action. Disabled actions remain focusable with aria-disabled, but cannot activate. They do not use native disabled, which would remove them from menu navigation.

DropdownMenu children can add custom buttons, links and noninteractive headers. Each custom action must use role=menuitem and tabindex=-1. Use aria-disabled=true for unavailable actions; the controller blocks them before target handlers run. Custom links retain native navigation, including keyboard activation. MenuItem callbacks and custom click handlers can preventDefault to keep the menu open. menuProps['@click'] can prevent dismissal after an action. menuProps['@keydown'] can prevent the built-in key behavior. These are synchronous event vetoes, not asynchronous authorization. Callback return values are ignored. These components implement single-level actions, not submenus, menu checkboxes or menu radios.

DropdownMenu opens on Enter, Space or pointer activation. ArrowDown opens at the first item and ArrowUp at the last. ContextMenu opens on right-click, Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key. Within a menu, Up/Down wrap, Home/End reach the ends, and printable characters perform prefix search with repeated-character cycling. Disabled actions participate in navigation. Tab and Shift+Tab close the menu and continue through the page from the invoker. Escape closes and returns focus. Action selection restores focus only while the menu still owns it, preserving focus when an action opens a dialog. Outside clicks retain their new focus target. If a focused item is removed during rendering, focus recovers to the first remaining item.

DropdownMenu uses a native auto popover. ContextMenu uses manual popover mode to avoid dismissal by the pointer gesture that opened it; its controller supplies outside-click and Escape dismissal. Context menus close when their surrounding document scrolls, but internal menu scrolling remains available. DropdownMenu respects disabled and inherited disabled fieldsets. ContextMenu uses its explicit disabled prop. showMenu()/closeMenu() remain available on DropdownMenu; hide() remains available on ContextMenu. Calls before connection or after cleanup do nothing. Menus require hydration for their keyboard behavior; SSR preserves stable IDs and named semantics.

DropdownMenu side and align describe preferred placement. Placement flips and clamps within the visual viewport, follows nested scrolling and resize, and uses RTL horizontal alignment. ContextMenu positions at the pointer or anchors to its context region for keyboard activation. Oversized panels scroll within viewport limits. menuProps.style can set width/height; the controller owns position, inset, top, left, margin, box-sizing, overflow and maximum viewport dimensions. Load the UI theme. Cleanup removes all document/viewport listeners and observers. Deferred setup is canceled if the component is removed before connection.

Published declarations, SSR and themed Chromium tests cover these contracts and installed CLI/MCP documentation. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the remaining UI/release matrix stay open.

guides.title: Tooltip and HoverCard ownership
guides.summary: Give hover content stable identities, keyboard access and explicit native attribute ownership.
guides.markdown:
Tooltip requires a page-unique, whitespace-free id and a nonempty plain-text label. The id identifies its role=tooltip panel. Put aria-describedby=id on the actual child trigger. Give that trigger its own accessible name and keyboard focus. Native attributes and @events target the outer span, not the trigger or panel. The wrapper adds no tab stop. Interactive content belongs in HoverCard rather than Tooltip.

HoverCard requires a page-unique id, a nonempty label naming its nonmodal dialog, and content. Its child trigger must be keyboard-focusable. Native attributes and @events target the outer div. contentProps targets the panel div; the component owns its id, role and accessible name. Tab follows native document order into interactive card content. Opening does not move focus, including when content has autofocus. Escape and explicit hide restore the trigger when the panel owns focus. show()/hide() are safe before connection and after cleanup.

Both components open immediately on child focus or after pointer hover delay (default 300 ms). closeDelay defaults to 150 ms. Delays must be integers from 0 through 60000. Content stays open while the pointer or focus remains inside the trigger or panel. Escape cancels pending opening and dismisses visible content until interest leaves. Outside pointer interaction dismisses it. disabled suppresses opening and closes visible content. Re-enabling needs a fresh interaction or an explicit HoverCard show(). Touch pointer entry does not open content.

Visual behavior requires JavaScript and the native Popover API. SSR supplies stable identities and the tooltip description relationship. Manual popovers escape ancestor clipping. side accepts top, bottom, left or right; Tooltip defaults to top and HoverCard to bottom. Position flips and clamps to the visual viewport, follows scroll and resize, and bounds oversized content. The controller owns fixed positioning, margin, inset, overflow and maximum dimensions. Cleanup cancels timers, observers, deferred setup and document listeners.

Published declarations, SSR, themed Chromium and Studio regression tests cover these contracts. Other browser engines and assistive-technology acceptance remain release work.

guides.title: AlertDialog confirmation ownership
guides.summary: Name confirmation dialogs, focus Cancel first and keep asynchronous actions application-owned.
guides.markdown:
AlertDialog requires a stable page-unique, whitespace-free id and a nonempty text title. description supplies the optional plain-text message. Derived title and description IDs name and describe the native role=alertdialog. The component owns role, aria-modal, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. Native attributes and @events target HTMLDialogElement; title is visible content rather than a native title attribute. cancelLabel and actionLabel must be nonempty localized strings. actionVariant is primary or destructive.

Use open for controlled state. Accept onClose by setting open=false; otherwise the native dialog reopens. Use defaultOpen for initial uncontrolled state. SSR renders closed; connection opens it modally. Cancel receives initial focus, the document outside is inert, and native dismissal restores prior focus. Backdrop clicks never dismiss. Escape dismisses unless closeOnEscape=false or a native @cancel callback prevents default. Cancel and close() request dismissal through the same controller. Calls before connection and after cleanup are safe. Prop-driven closing and cleanup do not emit onClose. Native @close still observes native close events.

onAction receives a native button event with HTMLButtonElement currentTarget. Confirmation does not automatically close or await a returned promise. The application owns pending state, errors and success. Set actionDisabled during pending work to prevent duplicate confirmation. Set controlled open=false after success, or call close() for an uncontrolled dialog. Cancellation does not undo or abort application work. onClose and native dialog listeners receive HTMLDialogElement currentTarget. Do not use visibility as authorization.

The native alert dialog pattern is documented at https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/. SSR, published types and themed Chromium cover this implementation. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the full release matrix remain separate acceptance work.

guides.title: Command search and shortcut ownership
guides.summary: Compose a named modal command palette with controlled state and deterministic shortcuts.
guides.markdown:
Command requires a stable page-unique id and a nonempty label naming the native modal dialog. items is a readonly array of CommandItem values with unique nonempty string IDs and nonempty labels. group supplies visible context; disabled items remain visible but cannot be selected. Native attributes and @events belong to HTMLDialogElement. The component owns the dialog name and modal semantics. Localize searchLabel, placeholder, emptyLabel and closeLabel.

Use open with onOpenChange for controlled state. The parent must accept each proposed state. Otherwise opening is ignored or native dismissal reopens the dialog. defaultOpen initializes uncontrolled state. setOpen(boolean) proposes a change. SSR renders a closed dialog and stable search/list relationships. Client connection opens it modally; the search field receives initial focus and outside content becomes inert. Close, Escape and backdrop interaction dismiss it, unless configured otherwise. Native @cancel can prevent Escape. Native @close observes browser close events; onOpenChange reports user state proposals rather than prop changes.

Search trims surrounding whitespace and uses case-insensitive label substring matching, not fuzzy matching. Focus remains in the named combobox while aria-activedescendant identifies a result. ArrowUp/Down wrap through enabled results; Enter selects one. Home/End and modified editing keys retain native text behavior. Composition Enter does not select. Empty and all-disabled results have no active descendant. Stable IDs preserve the highlighted result through reordering; removal falls back to the first enabled match. Pointer selection respects disabled state. Selection calls onSelect(id), then proposes closing. Return values and promises are not awaited; the application owns actions and errors. A thrown synchronous callback leaves the palette open. Search resets when accepted open state changes.

shortcut=true opts into Ctrl/Meta+K. It defaults to false. The first connected eligible Command in document order owns the shortcut; repeat, composition, Alt/Shift combinations and previously prevented events are ignored. Closed owners ignore shortcuts in input, textarea, select and contenteditable targets unless shortcutInEditable=true. Eligibility includes this rule, so an opted-in later owner can handle an editor shortcut when an earlier owner declines. The open palette can still toggle from its own search field. While a modal is open, only that modal is eligible. Use one app-level shortcut owner and explicit controls for local palettes. Do not add a competing document shortcut handler. Cleanup removes document listeners and registration, cancels queued connection work and closes the native dialog.

Published declarations, SSR and themed Chromium verify the component contract. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the full runtime matrix remain release work.

CommandItem also accepts a text description. It is exposed separately from the option name. grouped=true renders named groups in first-matching-group order, with enabled keyboard navigation following that exact visible order. Stable IDs still own the active result. renderItem can provide presentational content; item.label still owns search and the option name. Do not put interactive controls inside options. The CommandPalette block composes these capabilities rather than creating a second keyboard or dialog controller.

guides.title: Accordion and Collapsible ownership
guides.summary: Use named native buttons, stable panel relationships and explicit controlled disclosure state.
guides.markdown:
Accordion (also exported as AccordionItem) and Collapsible require a stable page-unique, whitespace-free id. Accordion summary and Collapsible trigger are nonempty text inside an owned native button. Do not pass a nested Button or interactive template as trigger content. Accordion headingLevel accepts 2 through 6 and defaults to 3. The heading contains the trigger, whose chevron is decorative. These components manage independent panels; they do not impose a single-open accordion group.

Native attributes and @events target the root div. triggerProps targets HTMLButtonElement; panelProps targets the outer content div. The component owns trigger type, ID, disabled state, aria-expanded and aria-controls. Root id derives id-trigger and id-panel. The panel owns its ID, animation style, inert, hidden and aria-hidden contracts. Give panelProps an appropriate role/name only when the content needs a landmark. Styling and listeners must use the target that owns them.

Use open and onToggle for controlled state. The parent must accept a proposed change. defaultOpen initializes uncontrolled state once; later changes do not reset it. Parent updates do not emit onToggle. Native Enter, Space and pointer activation toggle the button. triggerProps['@click'] runs first and can preventDefault to veto toggling. Other listeners and bubbling retain native behavior. disabled and inherited disabled fieldsets block activation; public toggle() also respects those states when connected. Trigger buttons never submit forms.

Closed panels remain mounted but are inert, hidden from accessibility and clipped to zero height. Closing while focus is inside returns focus to the enabled trigger before making the panel inert. Open panels finish at auto height with visible overflow, so changing content and overlays are not permanently clipped. Shared height animation supports reversal, reduced-motion preferences and browsers without Web Animations. Cleanup cancels running animations and releases refs. SSR renders the initial expanded/closed state and relationships; JavaScript is required for toggling.

Published types, SSR, themed Chromium and the existing animation tests cover these contracts. Source ejection includes disclosure helpers and imports native attribute types from the public UI package. Other browser engines, assistive technologies, application recipes and full runtime acceptance remain release work.

guides.title: Tabs selection, focus and identity
guides.summary: Keep controlled selection separate from roving focus with stable tab/panel relationships.
guides.markdown:
Tabs requires a stable page-unique id and a nonempty label naming the tab list. Native attributes and @events target the root div. listProps targets the list div; the component owns its ID, role, orientation, name and tabindex. Reserve the derived id-list, id-tab-encodedValue and id-panel-encodedValue identities. items accepts readonly TabsItem arrays with unique nonempty values. Text labels provide names; rich labels require nonempty ariaLabel and must contain only noninteractive presentation. Icons are decorative. Supply per-item content for distinct panels. All panels remain mounted while inactive panels are hidden.

Use value and onChange for controlled selection. The parent must accept a proposed value; a local interaction never overrides a later controlled value. defaultValue is captured once for uncontrolled state. A missing or disabled requested value falls back to the first enabled item without emitting a change. Empty/all-disabled items have no selected panel. Parent changes do not emit onChange. Item disabled state and native disabled fieldsets prevent activation. Values with punctuation are encoded for IDs and never interpolated into selectors.

activation defaults to automatic: keyboard focus proposes selection. manual keeps selection unchanged during arrow navigation until native Enter/Space activation. Pointer activation proposes selection once. Focus and selection remain separate when a controlled parent rejects a change. Horizontal arrows follow visual direction including RTL; vertical lists use Up/Down. Home/End reach the enabled ends. Navigation wraps and skips disabled buttons. Perpendicular arrows and modified/composing input retain native behavior. listProps['@keydown'] can prevent built-in behavior. Tab exits the tab list into the active panel. Native buttons never submit a form.

Keyed panels preserve input state. When reordering moves focused DOM, focus returns to the retained tab or panel control. Removing/disabling that tab or hiding its panel restores the selected enabled tab, or the tab list when none remain. Focus moved elsewhere is preserved. The single decorative indicator follows selected geometry through ResizeObserver, including label/font/size changes. Pill and underline variants support both orientations. Reduced motion disables indicator transitions. Cleanup disconnects observation and cancels queued connection/focus work.

SSR supplies initial selection, hidden panels and stable relationships. Visual indicator measurements and interaction require JavaScript. Published types, SSR and themed Chromium cover controlled/default state, rich labels, two-instance identity, focus, resize and cleanup. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and full release/runtime acceptance remain separate work.

guides.title: Toggle state and group selection
guides.summary: Use typed native toggle buttons with controlled values, stable defaults and keyboard focus separate from selection.
guides.markdown:
Toggle forwards native attributes and @events to HTMLButtonElement. It owns type=button and aria-pressed. Give its children a stable accessible name, or use aria-label for an icon-only button. Keep the name the same when pressed state changes. size accepts default, sm, lg or icon. Use pressed with onPressedChange for controlled state. The callback proposes a boolean; the parent must accept it. defaultPressed is captured once for uncontrolled state. A native @click handler can preventDefault to veto activation. Enter and Space use native button activation. Disabled buttons and enclosing disabled fieldsets block changes. Component state props do not become HTML attributes.

ToggleGroup requires a nonempty label naming its role=group root. Native attributes and @events target HTMLDivElement. Items use readonly ToggleGroupItem arrays with unique nonempty values. Omitted text labels fall back to the value. Rich labels require nonempty ariaLabel and must contain only noninteractive presentation. Native buttons own aria-pressed and type=button. Item disabled and group disabled block activation, as do disabled fieldsets. These are pressed buttons rather than radio inputs. They do not provide form values or reset with a form; supply application-owned hidden inputs or use RadioGroup for native form selection.

Single mode is the default. Its value/defaultValue and onChange argument are strings. Activating the selected item clears selection and emits an empty string. Multiple mode requires type=multiple and uses readonly string arrays for value/defaultValue; onChange receives a new mutable string array. Both modes are fully controlled when value is supplied, including SSR and parent changes. Use defaultValue for uncontrolled initial selection, captured once. Parent updates do not emit callbacks. Disabled and unknown selected values remain application-owned. Multiple changes preserve them and never mutate the supplied array. Callback arrays are separate from internal state, so callback mutation does not alter selection. If switching from multiple to single mode, only the first stored value is selected; provide a controlled value when the mode changes need another policy.

One enabled item participates in the tab order. Arrow keys wrap across enabled items and move focus without selecting. Horizontal direction follows RTL; vertical orientation uses Up/Down. Home/End focus the ends. Enter/Space toggle selection. The group @keydown handler can preventDefault to veto built-in navigation. Focus remembers the active item within the group, then returns the tab stop to a selected enabled item or the first enabled item after leaving. Keyed items retain identity during updates. Removing or disabling a focused item restores focus to a selected enabled item, the first enabled item, or the group when none are enabled. Intentional outside focus is preserved.

The single-mode indicator follows actual button size through ResizeObserver, including orientation and layout changes. Unknown selection hides it. Multiple mode highlights each selected button. Load the UI theme; reduced motion disables indicator transitions. Cleanup cancels deferred setup and disconnects observation. isSelected(value) reads the current selection; toggle(value) requests a change for an enabled item. Replace writes to the former selected field with value/onChange.

Renderer component() preserves mode-specific callback inference even when type=single is omitted. Published declaration tests, SSR, themed Chromium and source-ejection tests cover these contracts. Installed CLI/MCP catalogs expose the same guide and public types. This guide adds no standalone executable example; broader UI/runtime, other browser engine and assistive-technology acceptance remain release work.

guides.title: Menubar action navigation
guides.summary: Build a named application menubar with scoped identities, typed actions and owned keyboard focus.
guides.markdown:
Menubar requires a page-unique, whitespace-free id and a nonempty label. Native attributes and @events target the root HTMLDivElement. The component owns role=menubar, its name, orientation and roving focus. menus accepts readonly MenubarMenu arrays. Each menu requires a unique nonempty value and a nonempty text label. Use stable values while labels change or menus reorder. Derived trigger/menu IDs combine the instance id and encoded value. The component uses local element references rather than document-wide ID lookups.

Each menu accepts readonly MenuItem actions and separators, sharing the DropdownMenu/ContextMenu contract. Actions require nonempty text labels and can have disabled, destructive and onClick. onClick receives the native event with HTMLButtonElement currentTarget. A separator is {separator:true} and cannot also be an action. Menus and disabled actions remain keyboard-focusable with aria-disabled, but cannot activate. Enclosing disabled fieldsets still disable their native buttons. These are single-level action menus; nested submenus and checkbox/radio actions are not implemented. Use NavigationMenu for site links.

triggerProps targets each HTMLButtonElement. menuProps targets its HTMLDivElement panel. The component owns IDs, roles, relationships, trigger naming and disabled state. The panel name comes from its trigger. A trigger @click callback can preventDefault to veto opening. An action onClick or panel @click callback can preventDefault to keep the menu open. Root, trigger or panel @keydown callbacks can prevent built-in keyboard handling. Native event bubbling remains intact; callback return values are ignored. The application owns asynchronous work and authorization.

Tab enters one trigger and leaves the whole menubar/menu. Left/Right wrap between triggers using the current writing direction. Home/End reach the trigger ends. Enter/Space or Down opens at the first action; Up opens at the last. Within a menu, Up/Down, Home/End and prefix typeahead navigate actions. Left/Right switches to an adjacent menu; Escape returns to its trigger. Tab closes and continues from the trigger. Printable keys also search trigger labels. The last focused trigger remains the next tab stop. Hover switches menus only while a menu is already open, and touch pointer entry is ignored.

Native auto popovers supply outside dismissal. Closed panels expose no action tab stops. Action selection restores the trigger only while the menu still owns focus, preserving a new dialog or outside focus. Keyed menu updates retain focus. Removing a focused action returns to the first remaining action or panel; removing its menu returns to an available trigger or the root. The root is a programmatic fallback, not an extra tab stop. Menubar owns open state; the old public openMenu index is removed.

Panels flip and clamp within the viewport, follow scrolling/resize and bound oversized content with scrolling. Load the UI theme. Panel style can customize dimensions; the controller owns fixed position, inset, margin, overflow and maximum dimensions. Cleanup releases listeners/observers and cancels deferred setup. SSR renders the closed, named menubar with stable relationships; interaction requires hydration.

The keyboard model follows https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/. Published types, SSR, themed Chromium, ejected-source compilation and installed CLI/MCP discovery cover this implementation. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the full release matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no standalone executable example.

guides.title: Native navigation disclosures
guides.summary: Build named site navigation with stable sections, native links and focus-safe hover or click disclosures.
guides.markdown:
NavigationMenu requires a page-unique, whitespace-free id and a nonempty label naming the navigation landmark. Native attributes and @events target its HTMLElement root. sections accepts readonly NavigationMenuSection arrays. Each section needs a unique nonempty value and text label; each link needs a value unique within its section, a text label and a nonempty href. Optional descriptions are text. Keep values stable across translations and reorderings. Derived trigger/panel IDs combine the instance id and encoded section value. Local references keep instances independent.

triggerProps targets the native HTMLButtonElement, panelProps its HTMLDivElement, and linkProps the native HTMLAnchorElement. The component owns identities, disclosure relationships, trigger names and disabled state. AnchorAttributes includes target, rel, download, hreflang, referrerpolicy and ping. Links keep native URL, modifier and new-tab behavior. Root and section disabled props, plus native disabled fieldsets, disable triggers. These are navigation disclosures with ordinary links, not menu/menuitem widgets.

trigger defaults to hover; click opens only through activation. Both modes support native click, Enter and Space. hoverDelay defaults to 100 ms and closeDelay to 150 ms; both require integers from 0 to 60000. Hover never takes focus or dismisses another popup holding focus. Touch entry does not schedule hover. Pointer travel into the panel cancels closing; focused panel content stays open when the pointer leaves. Switching to click mode cancels pending hover timers.

Tab follows native buttons and visible links. Down/Up on a trigger opens at its first/last link, or the empty panel. Left/Right moves between enabled triggers using writing direction; Home/End reach the ends. Within a panel, Up/Down and Home/End navigate its links. Escape cancels pending opening, closes the panel and restores its trigger only while the panel owns focus. Outside pointer interaction or focus leaving the navigation closes it. A focus move within the navigation must not close the destination panel during native Tab transfer.

A trigger @click callback can preventDefault to veto opening. A link @click callback can veto selection and native navigation. Root, trigger and panel @keydown callbacks can veto built-in keyboard handling; callbacks receive native events with their declared currentTarget types. Ordinary unmodified link activation closes its panel. The application owns authorization and asynchronous effects.

Open state belongs to the native popovers; replace writes to the former activeSection index with ordinary activation. Keyed updates preserve focused links. Removing the focused link falls back to the first remaining link or panel; removing or disabling its section falls back to an enabled trigger or root. Updates preserve focus that has already moved elsewhere. The root and empty panel are programmatic fallbacks, not additional Tab stops.

Load the UI theme. Panels flip above when needed, clamp to the viewport, follow scrolling and resizing, and scroll oversized content. The component owns fixed positioning, inset, margin, overflow and maximum dimensions. Cleanup cancels timers and deferred connection and removes listeners and observers. SSR provides the named navigation, native links and stable relationships; disclosure interaction requires hydration.

The keyboard model follows https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/. Public types, SSR, themed Chromium, scaffold consumers, ejected-source compilation and installed CLI/MCP discovery are the focused acceptance targets. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the complete release matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no standalone executable example.

guides.title: Controlled pagination and native page links
guides.summary: Choose controlled page selection or native URL navigation with named controls and bounded rendering.
guides.markdown:
Pagination has two distinct contracts. For in-place data changes, provide page, totalPages and onPageChange. For URL navigation, provide page, totalPages and href(page), which returns a nonempty URL. Do not combine href with onPageChange. The component never owns data fetching or authorization. Use native URLs when a page has an address; scaffold users/roles lists now use this mode to preserve browser modifier keys and new tabs.

page is a positive safe integer. totalPages is a nonnegative safe integer; zero renders no numbered controls and disables Previous/Next. A page above a reduced count displays the last page without emitting a callback. The parent still owns its requested page and should reconcile it with its data. maxButtons is an integer from 1 through 100, default 5. It limits the sliding window, excluding first/last shortcuts and Previous/Next. Large counts do not allocate an array for every page. Gaps are decorative.

Native attributes and @events target the root HTMLElement navigation landmark. label names it, defaulting to Pagination. previousLabel and nextLabel default to Previous page and Next page. pageLabel(page) defaults to Page followed by its number. All names must be nonempty text; localize them in the application. The component owns the landmark role/name and programmatic fallback tabindex. Each current page has aria-current=page, and arrow icons are decorative and follow writing direction.

Button mode accepts buttonProps targeting each HTMLButtonElement. Controls use type=button and cannot submit surrounding forms. Native click, Enter and Space propose onPageChange once for a different enabled page. Activating the current page does not emit another request. Selection changes only when the parent updates page. A buttonProps @click callback receives the native event and can preventDefault to veto the proposal. disabled and enclosing disabled fieldsets block button activation. Callback return values are ignored; asynchronous work belongs to the application.

Link mode accepts linkProps targeting each HTMLAnchorElement, including target, rel, download and other native link attributes. href and accessible names remain owned by Pagination. Links retain normal navigation and modified-click behavior; a linkProps @click handler can preventDefault to veto native navigation. disabled or unavailable boundary links omit href, have aria-disabled=true, and leave the Tab order. Enclosing fieldsets do not disable native anchors: pass disabled when link pagination must be unavailable.

Tab follows ordinary enabled buttons or links. Pagination does not use a roving tab stop or capture arrow keys. Keyed numbered controls and fixed Previous/Next identities preserve focus as the window changes. Removing or disabling the focused control during a component update falls back to the displayed current page, another enabled control, or the root. Updates do not steal focus from elsewhere. Cleanup invalidates queued focus repair before remounting.

SSR provides native links, names, disabled boundaries and current-page semantics. Link navigation works without hydration; controlled button callbacks require hydration. Load the UI theme for focus rings, disabled styles and RTL arrows. Public declarations, SSR, themed Chromium, source ejection, scaffold recipes and installed CLI/MCP guidance provide focused acceptance. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the full framework/runtime matrix remain separate release work. This guide adds no standalone executable example.

The installed declaration catalog marks union props as partial and exposes a variants list. Inspect each variant to see whether href or onPageChange is required; the other field is forbidden. Shared members alone make both optional. Variant declarations do not prove runtime behavior.

guides.title: Named breadcrumb navigation
guides.summary: Render a stable hierarchy with native links, a current-page marker and typed native attribute targets.
guides.markdown:
Breadcrumb renders a navigation landmark containing an ordered list. label names the landmark and defaults to Breadcrumb; localize it in the application. Root native attributes and @events target HTMLElement. listProps targets HTMLOListElement. The component owns root role/name and its programmatic fallback tabindex. separator is decorative text, defaults to / and can be empty. Separators are hidden from the accessibility tree.

items accepts readonly BreadcrumbItem arrays in hierarchy order. Each item requires a unique nonempty value that remains stable across translation, reorder and URL changes. Text labels supply accessible names. Rich labels require nonempty ariaLabel and must contain noninteractive presentation only. For unlinked rich text, the visual label is hidden from the accessibility tree and the supplied name is rendered as screen-reader text. Do not put buttons, links or inputs inside labels.

An item with a nonempty href renders a native anchor, including the final item. It accepts linkProps with HTMLAnchorElement events and native target, rel, download and related attributes. An item without href renders a span and accepts textProps with HTMLSpanElement events. Do not mix those targets. BreadcrumbLinkProps, BreadcrumbTextProps and BreadcrumbListProps name these public contracts. The component owns href, item names, tabindex and current-page semantics. Native @click handlers can preventDefault to veto link navigation; callback return values do not cancel it.

The final item has aria-current=page whether linked or plain text. Earlier items have no current-page marker. An empty trail renders an empty ordered list with no current item. Tab and Shift+Tab follow native links; arrow keys are not captured. Links keep native Enter activation, modified clicks and new-tab behavior. Link navigation works before hydration.

Keyed items preserve focus when the hierarchy reorders. If the focused link disappears or becomes plain text, focus returns to the first remaining visible link or the navigation root. Updates preserve focus that has already moved elsewhere. Cleanup invalidates queued focus repair and releases element references. The root fallback is not an extra Tab stop. Load the UI theme for link focus rings and visually hidden text.

The semantics follow https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/. The demo and scaffold blog layout use stable values; the blog derives its trail from the current request path and keeps translated labels separate from identity. Public types, SSR, themed Chromium, accessibility snapshots, scaffold recipes, source ejection and installed CLI/MCP discovery provide focused acceptance. Other browser engines, assistive technologies, generated-app navigation and the full release matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Button groups, separators and aspect ratios
guides.summary: Use typed native wrappers for named control groups, static dividers and responsive media sizing.
guides.markdown:
ButtonGroup requires a nonempty label naming its native div group. Native attributes and @events target HTMLDivElement. orientation is horizontal by default or vertical. The component owns role=group, the name and data-orientation. It adds no Tab stop, arrow-key navigation, selection state or child event handlers. Use ToggleGroup for selection and a toolbar component/pattern when toolbar keyboard behavior is required.

Load the UI base stylesheet and theme. Direct native button and anchor children have joined borders, with logical corners and margins supporting RTL and vertical groups. The focused child is raised so adjacent borders do not cover its focus ring. Nested wrappers and mixed non-control children are not joined. Children retain their own names, types, disabled state, form behavior, URLs and callbacks. Set type=button on children that should not submit forms. Use native disabled buttons or fieldsets; naming a group does not authorize or disable actions.

Separator is a static divider. Its default horizontal form is a native hr, with HTMLHRElement event targets. orientation=vertical renders a div with role=separator and aria-orientation=vertical, with HTMLDivElement event targets. decorative=true hides either form using aria-hidden=true; the decorative vertical form omits the separator role and orientation. False omits aria-hidden. The component owns role, orientation, hidden state and tabindex. It has no keyboard interaction or adjustable value; use Resizable for an interactive splitter. Vertical separators stretch inside a flex container with a defined height. Load the theme for border colors and sizing.

AspectRatio forwards native attributes and events to an outer HTMLDivElement. ratio is a positive finite width/height number and defaults to 1. Invalid ratios reject before rendering. An inner box uses native CSS aspect-ratio and takes the wrapper's available width; an absolute content layer fills that box. Outer styles such as width, max-width, padding and borders remain independent from the inner ratio rule. Explicit outer height can constrain or overflow the inner box according to normal CSS. Supply the child image's alt text and object-fit styling yourself. The wrapper does not imply image semantics. This replaces percentage padding, which was based on the containing block rather than the wrapper's own width.

All three controls render their semantics and layout during SSR without JavaScript. Hydration attaches supplied native callbacks. They create no global listeners or observers. Public types, SSR, themed production Chromium, ejected-source compilation and installed CLI/MCP guidance cover the reviewed contracts. The browser checks joined borders, focus rings, native keyboard/form behavior, disabled fieldsets, decorative separator exposure and responsive ratio dimensions. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and the full release matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Loading placeholders and display surfaces
guides.summary: Use typed decorative Skeletons, native Card slots, text badges and keyboard descriptions.
guides.markdown:
Skeleton is decorative: it always has aria-hidden=true, renders no children and does not enter Tab order. Put loading text and aria-busy on the containing content region. Rectangle mode uses width and height; defaults are 100% and 1em, so an omitted height remains visible. Circle mode uses circle=true and one size, defaulting to 1em. Do not combine circle size with width/height. SkeletonDimension accepts nonnegative finite pixel numbers or nonempty CSS length/expression strings. The browser interprets CSS strings; the component does not parse the CSS language. Zero is allowed when deliberately collapsing a shape.

Native attributes and @events target the Skeleton HTMLDivElement. Generated dimensions are composed with a supplied style string or ifDefined style. Supplied CSS is appended and can deliberately override dimensions. Optional/omitted styles retain generated dimensions. The UI theme supplies pulse animation; prefers-reduced-motion disables it. A skeleton is not a focusable progress indicator or an action.

Card, CardHeader, CardBody and CardFooter all expose typed HTMLDivElement attributes and native events. CardHeaderProps, CardBodyProps and CardFooterProps name the slot contracts. Headings and actions belong in children: the slots do not supply heading levels, button semantics, keyboard activation or authorization. Card padding affects the Card root only, with none/sm/default/lg values. Header/body/footer slots retain their own spacing. Use padding=none when composing already padded slots, as in the components demo; plain content can use the default root padding.

Card hoverable requests only a visual shadow/lift effect. It replaces the misleading interactive name, adds no pointer cursor or Tab stop, and disables lift/transitions under reduced motion. Put native buttons or links inside the card for actions; a native link can wrap a card containing only noninteractive content. Native div @click callbacks remain native listeners and do not supply keyboard activation. Callback return values do not synthesize activation behavior.

Badge forwards native props and events to HTMLSpanElement. variant selects a supported color treatment; unsupported values reject early. Badge adds no live region, button behavior or focus stop. Supply readable status text so color is not the only information; use native live-region attributes on an appropriate region when announcements are needed.

Kbd forwards native props and events to HTMLElement on a kbd tag. It describes a key or key combination and registers no shortcut. Supply readable key text or a visually hidden expansion for symbols. Actual shortcut handling belongs to Command or the application. Both Badge and Kbd preserve supplied children and native event bubbling.

All seven exports render during SSR; the four source rows include every Card slot. Public declaration tests, SSR, themed Chromium, ejected-source compilation and installed CLI/MCP guidance cover their reviewed contracts. Browser checks default/circle dimensions, native style composition, reduced motion, root/slot padding, native child actions and link navigation, event targets and cleanup/remounting. Other browser engines, assistive technologies, the blocks audit and the full release matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Alerts, progress and loading status
guides.summary: Choose announcement urgency, name determinate or unknown progress, and use native SVG loading indicators.
guides.markdown:
Alert forwards typed attributes and @events to an HTMLDivElement. announcement defaults to assertive (role=alert), polite uses role=status, and off omits a live role for static content. Tone does not select urgency. Use urgent announcements sparingly. The component never moves focus or automatically dismisses content. Keep actions as native child buttons/links; an alert is not a dialog. title is visible message text, not a native tooltip attribute. Import an IconEntry for icon; null removes the icon and omission selects the variant icon. Icons are decorative; include meaning in text. Live roles do not guarantee that initial server-rendered content will be announced. Keep an existing region mounted and update its content when practical.

Progress requires a nonempty label naming its native div progressbar. Native @events target HTMLDivElement. value is a finite number clamped to 0..max; omitted or null value means unknown progress and omits aria-valuenow. Zero is determinate zero progress. max defaults to 100 and must be positive and finite. valueText optionally supplies nonempty human-readable progress. Component-owned name, role and numeric ARIA attributes cannot be overridden by native props. It has no Tab stop or value-changing keyboard behavior. The parent owns work, completion, retries and announcements. Place interactive controls outside the progressbar because its children are presentational. Do not announce each numeric update as an urgent alert. The unknown state has a full-width shimmer rather than implying a measured percentage. Reduced motion removes shimmer and width transitions. The surrounding content region owns aria-busy when appropriate.

Spinner retains an SVGSVGElement root with typed native SVG @events, class/style, ARIA and data attributes. HTML-only props are rejected. size and stroke must be finite with size > stroke > 0; size defaults to 20 and stroke to 2. Its owned geometry, focusability and role cannot be replaced by spread props. Without label it is decorative and aria-hidden; when a nonempty label is supplied it uses role=status, aria-label and title text. The SVG never enters the Tab order. Update the label to describe current work; omit it when nearby status text already announces that work. Reduced motion stops rotation. Status semantics do not prove speech delivery for any assistive technology.

All three controls render with SSR and hydrate native callbacks without observers or global listeners. Load the UI base stylesheet and theme for sizing, colors and motion rules. Public types, SSR tests, themed Chromium, source ejection and installed CLI/MCP guidance cover their reviewed contracts. Other browser engines, screen readers and the full runtime matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Linked fields and empty states
guides.summary: Render a named native control with shared description attributes, and preserve native empty-state actions.
guides.markdown:
Field requires a nonempty label, a unique control ID in for (without whitespace), and a control callback. The callback receives readonly FieldControlAttributes: id, required, aria-describedby and aria-invalid. Spread them onto the actual input, select or textarea. Input and PasswordInput forward these attributes to their native input. For example: component(Field, { label: 'Email', for: 'email', hint: 'Use work email', error, required: true, control: attributes => component(Input, { ...attributes, type: 'email', name: 'email', '.value': value }) }). The callback owns the control type, value/binding, events, name, disabled state and submission behavior. Keep it synchronous and free of side effects. Separate third-argument children are rejected rather than silently dropped.

The wrapper's native props and @events target HTMLDivElement. The wrapper id is independent of for; do not reuse a control ID on the wrapper or another element. The visible label targets for. Nonempty hint and error text render together, using <for>-hint and <for>-error IDs; aria-describedby contains both IDs in that order. Empty or whitespace-only messages are absent. aria-invalid is true only while error text is present. required supplies the visual marker and the boolean passed to the control. The marker is hidden from accessibility naming so the actual native required state describes the requirement. A callback that discards or overrides these attributes breaks the relationship; the library does not inspect, clone or mutate its returned controls. To add another description, merge its ID with the supplied aria-describedby value.

Field is for one native labelable control. Use fieldset/legend for control groups and explicit naming for custom widgets. It does not register validation rules, setCustomValidity, submit or reset a form, move focus, announce each error, or infer error timing. aria-invalid does not change native validity. The form/controller owns touched/submitted state, error summaries and server validation. Native disabled fieldsets and form behavior remain intact. Avoid competing child IDs or required flags; put shared required state on Field.

Empty forwards typed native div attributes and events, including id, class, style, ARIA and data attributes. title and description render visible paragraphs; title is not a native tooltip attribute or implied heading. icon accepts renderer content; supply aria-hidden for a decorative illustration or an appropriate alternative for meaningful media. Empty does not hide all illustrations automatically because their meaning belongs to the caller. Put real buttons and links in children, with their own names, types, URLs and callbacks. Use type=button for actions that should not submit a surrounding form. Empty adds no implicit role, focus stop, click action or live announcement. The parent owns search, retry, loading and dynamic notification behavior.

Public declarations, SSR, themed production Chromium, source ejection, generated login rendering and installed CLI/MCP guidance cover these contracts. Browser checks include label focus, descriptions, native validation/FormData, password reveal, disabled fieldsets, child buttons/links, focus-preserving updates and cleanup. Other engines, screen readers and the complete generated-app/runtime matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Named avatars and stable avatar groups
guides.summary: Keep image failures scoped to their source, retain accessible fallback names, and key grouped avatars by stable values.
guides.markdown:
Avatar requires alt text. Use a meaningful name for informative portraits or an explicit empty string for decoration. The root span retains role=img and the trimmed name even when the image fails; its nested image and visual initials are hidden from accessibility naming to avoid duplicate announcements. Decorative avatars hide their whole noninteractive content. Fallback children may be noninteractive visual content; do not put buttons, links or focusable descendants inside an avatar. The parent owns native links/buttons when a portrait is actionable. Initials use the first Unicode code point of up to two whitespace-separated words; the full alternative text remains the accessible name.

Native attributes and @events target HTMLSpanElement. onImageLoad/onImageError receive the real HTMLImageElement event target. loading, decoding and referrerpolicy apply to the image. Size must be positive and finite; shape is circle or square. Generated width/height/font size compose with native style, including ifDefined; supplied style follows generated declarations. Role, name, hidden state and focus attributes belong to the component. A click handler does not add keyboard activation.

Each changed source gets a new request identity and image node. Failure belongs to that request; changing src retries, including switching away and back to a previously failed URL. Detached/stale image events cannot hide the current image or invoke its callbacks. A queued complete/naturalWidth check handles images that failed before hydration. It does not synthesize missed load/error events: callbacks observe native events received after listeners attach. Clearing src displays fallback content. Without JavaScript the server renders the image URL and stable accessible name; network-error initials require hydration. Cleanup invalidates queued checks and old event ownership. The browser still owns network fetching and caching.

AvatarGroup requires a label and readonly items with unique nonempty value keys, alt text and optional src. Keys identify people independently of position or name.
