It preserves each Avatar's DOM/state during reordering. max is a nonnegative safe integer (default 5); zero displays only overflow. size is positive and finite. overlap is now a nonnegative number smaller than size, defaulting to size/4; it is converted to negative logical margins. direction supports row and row-reverse, with logical edges supporting inherited RTL. ring controls the separating box shadow. Root native props/events target HTMLDivElement. It adds no selection or focus behavior.

Hidden items produce a visible +N and readable overflow text; overflowLabel(count) customizes and localizes that nonempty text. The default is 'N more people'. It describes the count, not hidden identities. Supply a separate member list or named action when users need those identities. Empty groups retain their name and no counter. Label, role and item geometry are component-owned; authored CSS can intentionally override styles.

Public types, SSR, themed Chromium, strict source-ejection compilation and installed CLI/MCP guidance cover these contracts. Browser coverage includes failure before hydration, URL recovery, stale image events, live image callbacks, accessible fallback names, native targets, keyed reorder, RTL/reverse geometry, zero/empty groups and cleanup. Other browsers, screen readers and the full runtime matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Semantic typography and native list-row actions
guides.summary: Choose native typography variants and keep Item hover styling separate from child controls.
guides.markdown:
Typography has six native prop branches covering thirteen visual variants. Omitted variant, p, lead and muted render HTMLParagraphElement; h1/h2/h3/h4 render HTMLHeadingElement; blockquote renders HTMLQuoteElement and accepts cite; ol renders HTMLOListElement and accepts start, reversed and type; ul renders HTMLUListElement; code/kbd/small render HTMLElement. Native @events target that actual element. Invalid variants reject rather than silently falling back. Quote and ordered-list attributes are excluded from incompatible variants, including the default paragraph.

Choose headings for document structure, not just font size. Paragraph and inline variants require appropriate phrasing content. Put li elements directly inside ul/ol; do not pass bare text or Item divs as their direct children. Ordered lists preserve start and reversed and map type=1/a/A/i/I to decimal, lower-alpha, upper-alpha, lower-roman and upper-roman markers despite the theme reset. Optional ifDefined type attributes use the same mapping. Authored CSS can override marker styling. Blockquote cite is source metadata, not a visible citation link; add a readable link separately when needed. code renders inline code; compose pre/code for multiline blocks. kbd describes keys and installs no shortcuts. Typography adds no interaction or focus management. Native child links and supplied attributes retain their own behavior.

Item forwards closed native div attributes/events. media, children and trailing remain renderer content slots. hoverable replaces interactive and adds only hover colors/transitions; it does not install click/keyboard behavior, a pointer cursor, button role or a Tab stop. Reduced motion removes the color transition. divider and compact control the bottom border and vertical padding. Boolean flags must be booleans. Root callbacks receive HTMLDivElement; slot content owns its own native callbacks and names.

Use a native link in the main content and a native type=button action in trailing for rows with multiple actions. A whole-row native link may wrap an Item only when its contents contain no other interactive controls. Put Item inside li when using a native list. A visual hover style does not supply menu, listbox or selection semantics. Media alternatives and action accessibility belong to the caller. Fields, validation, URLs and form submission remain native child responsibilities.

Public types, SSR, themed Chromium, strict source ejection and installed CLI/MCP metadata cover all thirteen Typography variants and the Item wrapper. Browser checks semantic headings/lists, actual event targets, list marker types, native Tab/Enter/link behavior, independent actions without form submission, dynamic variants, spacing and reduced motion. Other engines, screen readers and the full runtime matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Native tables and scroll viewports
guides.summary: Compose typed table sections and give scrollable content an explicit name, keyboard access and correctly targeted events.
guides.markdown:
Table is a native table inside an overflow div. Top-level id, class, style, ARIA and @event props now target HTMLTableElement. Use wrapperProps for attributes, sizing and listeners on the outer HTMLDivElement. Give the table a caption or an accessible name. For a wide table, wrapperProps can supply tabindex:0, role:region and a short aria-label so keyboard users can scroll horizontally. Choose whether this extra focus stop is useful for your content. Table does not add grid navigation or row selection. Put actions in child links and buttons with explicit types.

Pass a caption and explicit thead/tbody sections as children. Compose TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead and TableCell with component(), or use native markup. Each helper forwards typed props and @event listeners to its actual native element. TableHeader and TableBody target HTMLTableSectionElement, TableRow targets HTMLTableRowElement, and both cell helpers target HTMLTableCellElement. Use lowercase colspan, rowspan and headers on cells. scope and abbr belong to TableHead. TableCellAttributes and TableHeadAttributes are public types. Authors own header IDs, scope and headers relationships, caption text and valid HTML content models. A fragment containing rows still needs an explicit table section; the component does not repair invalid table markup.

striped:true colors even body rows using the UI theme. TableRow respects reduced motion for hover transitions. Table applies default cell padding and header styling to native children. Load the UI theme and include component sources in Tailwind scanning as for the rest of the package.

ScrollArea now renders one div: both cs-scroll-area and cs-scroll-area__viewport refer to the actual viewport. A nonempty label is required and owns its region name. The viewport defaults to tabindex:0 for keyboard scrolling. Use tabindex:-1 only when another control supplies keyboard access. height accepts a nonnegative finite pixel number or a nonempty CSS length/expression, including auto. Browser CSS parsing owns validity of string values. Authored style follows generated height and overflow styles and can override them. class merges with the component classes. @scroll receives the actual scrolling HTMLDivElement, so read event.currentTarget.scrollTop or scrollLeft synchronously. Ordinary scroll events do not bubble; a listener on a separate parent is not equivalent.

Public declaration, SSR, themed Chromium hydration and source-ejection checks cover these contracts, native child actions and scrolling in both directions. The installed catalog describes props and event targets. This guide is not an executable example, and other browsers, assistive technologies and the full generated-app/runtime matrix remain separate acceptance work.

guides.title: Accessible two-panel resizing
guides.summary: Use named panels, bounded percentages, controlled or local state, and keyboard/pointer resizing with cleanup.
guides.markdown:
Resizable requires a stable document-unique id, a nonempty label, and explicit primary and secondary renderer values. Pass panel content in those props, not component() children. label names the primary group and adjustable separator. Derived IDs are id-primary, id-secondary and id-handle; the separator controls the primary panel. Top-level native props and events target the root HTMLDivElement. primaryProps, secondaryProps and handleProps target separate divs. ResizablePanelProps and ResizableHandleProps are public. Relationship IDs, collapsed visibility, separator values and its keyboard/pointer handlers belong to the component. Use onSizeChange for resize changes and handleProps for supported native attributes/focus events.

Give the root a usable height. It uses two grid tracks with a six-pixel handle between them. size is the primary percentage of the space left after the handle; the other panel gets the remainder. minSize defaults to 10 and bounds both panels, so the default range is 10 to 90. It must be finite and between 0 and 50. minSize:50 fixes both panels equally and disables the handle. size and defaultSize must be finite percentages from 0 to 100, then clamp to the current bounds. Strings, NaN and Infinity are rejected. Root style follows generated layout styles; overriding layout tracks, handle dimensions or panel geometry can invalidate these sizing guarantees. Load the UI theme and scan the component sources with Tailwind.

Omit size for local state. defaultSize is captured once, defaults to 50, and later changes do not reset the component. Returning to 50 after a drag does not restore an old default. Supply size for controlled state; onSizeChange proposes a bounded percentage and the caller must acknowledge it by updating size. A controlled caller can reject a proposal by leaving size unchanged. Constraint changes clamp displayed size without emitting a callback from render. Callbacks run on user resize changes, not initial render or unchanged boundary attempts.

orientation is the panel layout: horizontal means side-by-side panels and a vertical separator; vertical means stacked panels and a horizontal separator. Focus the handle with Tab. Arrow keys move it on the layout axis; horizontal movement follows the root's actual text direction. step defaults to one percentage point and Shift multiplies it by ten. Home and End select the allowed bounds. Enter minimizes to minSize and restores the previous position, or 50 when there is no larger position to restore. With minSize:0, an endpoint can fully collapse a panel; collapsed content is inert and hidden from assistive technology, and focus inside that panel moves to the handle. disabled removes the handle from Tab order and prevents resize proposals. Native links and buttons inside panels retain their own behavior.

A primary pointer drag uses pointer capture on the handle. Mouse and touch have browser acceptance; unrelated pointers cannot move an active drag. Pointer up/cancel, lost capture, window blur, unmount, disabling, orientation/limit/ID changes and synchronous callback failures release owned resources. A change to computed text direction cancels on the next movement. No document cursor or selection styles are modified. Geometry is measured at drag start; avoid changing panel layout dimensions during a drag. Application callbacks own their external effects and asynchronous failures.

Public declaration, SSR, themed Chromium hydration, mouse/touch interaction, controlled rejection/acceptance, RTL, vertical layout, default capture, endpoint focus and interruption checks cover this contract. Source-ejected code compiles with public imports. Installed CLI/MCP catalogs expose props and guide text. Other browsers, assistive technologies, the generated-app/runtime matrix and executable coverage for this guide remain separate release work.

guides.title: Named Sidebar navigation and collapsed modes
guides.summary: Use stable nested items, native links and disclosures, controlled collapse, and explicit offcanvas focus ownership.
guides.markdown:
Sidebar requires a stable document-unique id and a nonempty label for its navigation landmark. Top-level native props/events target the aside (HTMLElement); navProps target the nav (HTMLElement). title is visual brand text, and brand replaces it. footer is a renderer slot. Pass navigation in items, not component() children. SidebarNavProps and SidebarLinkProps are public; the latter targets HTMLAnchorElement. Derived nav/group IDs, names, current-page state and disclosure controls belong to the component. A sidebar is navigation with lists and native disclosures, not an ARIA menu.

Every item has a globally unique nonempty value and nonempty label. Values must remain stable across reordering, filtering and translation. A leaf requires href. A group requires a nonempty readonly children array, supports nested groups and may also have href; that destination remains a link inside its disclosed content. SidebarItem, SidebarLinkItem and SidebarGroupItem are public types. Duplicate values and cycles reject before rendering. active marks a current-page link and opens its ancestors by default. Before a group is manually toggled, its default expansion follows active descendants; an explicit user choice, including closed, takes precedence and follows the group's value. Authors own the accuracy of current-page flags and destinations.

Groups use details/summary, so disclosures and links work without JavaScript. With hydration, Tab, Enter and Space retain native summary activation; Escape closes the nearest open group and restores its summary focus. Reordering retains keyed elements; removed/hidden focused content recovers to a reachable replacement or the sidebar toggle/nav. Native child actions remain independent. Icon mode is a 72-pixel rail: visible labels become screen-reader text, icons are decorative, and an initial letter appears when no icon is supplied. Nested links remain reachable by opening their groups. A native title provides a pointer tooltip. Icon mode does not replace child links with placeholder hrefs or require hover to open them.

collapsed remains caller-controlled. onToggle receives the proposed next boolean; the caller must update collapsed. Omit onToggle to omit the built-in button. expandLabel and collapseLabel customize/localize its text. width is a nonempty CSS string. Root styles compose with generated dimensions, so authored overrides own their layout effects. The UI theme supplies rail, border and transition styling; include component sources in Tailwind scanning. Logical spacing supports RTL, and reduced motion removes width transitions.

Offcanvas mode requires collapsible:offcanvas and restoreFocusTo, the ID of a focusable opener outside the sidebar. The caller creates this opener and maintains aria-controls pointing to the Sidebar id and aria-expanded matching its state. Hiding focused sidebar content restores that opener first, then sets hidden/inert and removes the sidebar from layout. A missing or unfocusable opener rejects that focus transition. Opening does not take focus automatically. Escape requests offcanvas collapse when no open group consumes it. This is not modal behavior: use Sheet for modal focus containment and overlays. The application owns responsive placement and external trigger visibility.

Links accept linkProps such as target, rel, download, data/ARIA attributes and @click. Item label owns the accessible name and active owns aria-current. Without onNavigate they keep native navigation. With onNavigate, only an unmodified primary-button click on a same-origin HTTP(S) link with a self target and no download is intercepted. Named targets, new tabs, base target, modifier clicks, external origins and other protocols retain browser behavior. A linkProps listener can prevent default first. The callback receives the item and a typed native anchor event; capture currentTarget before awaiting. The application owns enhanced routing and callback failures.

Public types, SSR, themed Chromium, real popup/download behavior, nested disclosures, collapsed modes, focus recovery and source-ejection checks cover this foundation. The generated dashboard render fixture uses the real UI contract with stable module IDs and explicit naming. Installed CLI/MCP catalogs expose both collapse-mode branches and this guide. Other engines, assistive technologies and the full generated-app/runtime matrix remain separate release gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Toast stores, announcements and owned timers
guides.markdown:
Mount one Toaster in the browser application root, then call toast.show, toast.success, toast.warning or toast.error from a client handler. toast and toastStore are the same default store. All mutations and subscriptions require a browser; server methods must return results that a client handler can turn into a notification. Calling a toast method on the server throws before changing its queue. Importing the module and rendering Toaster on the server remain safe and produce an empty region with a permanent live announcer. This is transient UI state, not a durable notification service or a server-to-browser transport.

createToastStore({maxToasts:5}) creates an isolated store for a separate application region or test. Pass that same instance as Toaster's store prop. The bound must be an integer from 1 to 100; a full queue rejects new messages without evicting focused content. Each store permits one mounted presenter. Store identity cannot change while mounted; unmount before replacing it. Messages queued before mounting have no timers until a presenter connects. Unmount cancels timers and clears that presenter's queue, but does not permanently dispose the store. dispose permanently empties an isolated store and releases its subscribers; subsequent mutations and subscriptions reject. Do not dispose the shared default store. get returns a frozen readonly snapshot and subscribe receives the initial snapshot plus changes; call its returned function to unsubscribe. set/update are deliberately absent. Use show, dismiss(id) or clear instead. Subscriber failures are reported after every current subscriber receives the update; mutations already committed are not rolled back.

ToastOptions accepts duration and variant only. Message text must be nonempty; it renders as text. IDs are generated by the store. ToastItem fields are readonly. Variants are default, success, warning and destructive. The success/warning/error helpers accept only duration and choose their own variant. Duration is a finite millisecond number from 0 to 2147483647, defaulting to 4000; zero is persistent. Timers measure elapsed time while the presenter is active. Hovering or focusing its region, window blur, and a hidden document pause all its countdowns, including new messages. Resuming preserves the remaining duration. Dismissal cancels the corresponding timer. Use duration:0 for information that is not available elsewhere, or provide a user preference or another persistent view; hover/focus pause alone is not a general time-limit accessibility solution.

Toaster root attributes/events target an HTMLDivElement. It owns role, tab order, accessible name and live-region behavior. label defaults to Notifications and dismissLabel defaults to Dismiss; localize them through props. Each native type=button dismissal control has a name formed from dismissLabel and the message. Its activation never submits a containing form. Escape dismisses the focused toast. Adding a message does not move focus. Removing a focused toast moves focus to a remaining dismissal button, the previously focused external element, or the notification region. The visible ordered list is separate from one permanent polite status announcer. The announcer marks additions relevant and disables atomic repetition of the whole queue; removed messages do not request announcements. Real assistive-technology behavior still needs release acceptance.

Positions are top-right, top-left, bottom-right, bottom-left and bottom-center. The responsive stack fits narrow viewports, uses logical close-button placement and wraps message text. The UI theme disables entrance animation for reduced motion. Include UI sources in Tailwind scanning. Toaster accepts no component children. Native style/class overrides remain the caller's responsibility.

Public types, server-mutation rejection, immutable isolated queues, SSR, themed Chromium lifecycle/timing/focus tests and source-ejection compilation cover this foundation. These checks do not replace the generated-app and full runtime matrix. This guide adds no executable example.
guides.summary: Use isolated browser notification stores with owned timers, native dismissal, focus recovery and one polite announcer.

guides.title: Named Carousel slides and native scrolling
guides.summary: Navigate stable slides with native scroll targets, compact sizing, keyboard and RTL behavior, focus recovery and owned observers.
guides.markdown:
Carousel requires a stable document-unique id, a nonempty label and a readonly slides array. Each CarouselSlide has a unique nonempty value, an accessible label and explicit content as a renderer value. Pass content inside each slide, not as component() children. Empty arrays are supported. Duplicate identities, missing content and empty required names reject before rendering. Item values remain stable across sorting, removal and translation. The demo uses compact cards through slideSize:12rem.

Native root attributes and events target the outer HTMLDivElement, named as a carousel region. viewportProps targets the separate scrollable HTMLDivElement. Each slide's props targets its own HTMLDivElement. CarouselSlide, CarouselSlideProps and CarouselViewportProps are public types. The component owns root/viewport/slide IDs, roles and accessible labels, and the viewport tab stop. Derived IDs are id-viewport and id-slide-encodedValue. Caller aria-roledescription can localize the root or a slide's default description. viewportLabel defaults to Slides, previousLabel to Previous slide, nextLabel to Next slide and emptyLabel to No slides. Localize these strings as needed. Native caller handlers run before internal handlers; preventing a cancelable viewport key event suppresses Carousel keyboard navigation.

slideSize is a nonempty CSS flex-basis string, defaulting to 100%. An individual slide's size overrides it. Use percentages, rem or pixel lengths to retain compact multi-card layouts. The component adds min-width:0 and composes a slide's authored style after its sizing styles. Use valid CSS and contain oversized child content; overriding layout styles owns the resulting geometry. Controls use the actual scroll range, including native content overflow. Both become unavailable when all content fits. Unavailable controls use aria-disabled and remain focusable; activation does not move or wrap past a boundary. The component never starts automatic rotation.

The viewport and slides remain in native reading and focus order. Without JavaScript, native scrolling and Tab navigation into slide content still work; button and enhanced keyboard navigation require hydration. With the viewport itself focused, horizontal arrows follow physical direction, including RTL; Home and End target the first and last slide. Keys inside inputs, links or nested controls retain their native behavior. Native Tab can move into every slide. Focusing content brings its slide into view when needed. Reordering retains keyed elements and the visible identity; removing the selected slide uses the nearest remaining ordinal. Removed focused content recovers to the viewport. Moving the viewport away from focused content recovers focus after scrolling settles. Buttons retain focus during navigation.

Browser methods scrollNext, scrollPrev and scrollToSlide(value) navigate actual slide geometry instead of a fixed viewport fraction. Unknown scrollToSlide values throw in the browser. Calls while disconnected are harmless for valid values. Rapid requests advance from the pending destination. Pointer/wheel interaction interrupts a pending smooth scroll. Reduced motion uses instant movement, including when the preference changes during a pending movement. Viewport and slide ResizeObservers retain the selected identity during geometry changes; inherited direction changes are observed too. Unmount removes observers and listeners and cancels pending frames and settlement timers. Callback failures and external application effects remain caller-owned.

onValueChange reports the settled visible anchor, not a controlled-state proposal or an awaited scrolling operation. The anchor is the slide nearest the viewport's leading edge; at the scroll end it is the last slide, and when all slides fit it is the first. Compact layouts can show several slides at once. The callback receives undefined when the list becomes empty. Initial mounting does not emit a value change. A polite status announces the settled position and label. A short quiet interval detects settlement; no browser scrollend event is required. A parent must rerender after changing the slides array. The component does not hide offscreen slide content from assistive technology or remove its native tab stops.

Public types, SSR, a real themed Chromium fixture, no-JavaScript native focus, full and compact layouts, nested controls, caller event veto, focus/reorder recovery, dynamic content, RTL, resizing, reduced motion and source-ejection compilation cover this foundation. These checks do not establish full assistive-technology or cross-browser acceptance and do not replace generated-app/runtime release gates. Include UI sources in Tailwind scanning and load the UI theme. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Named attachments and native removal
guides.summary: Forward native file-card, removal-button and thumbnail props with explicit localized status styling and caller-owned removal.
guides.markdown:
Attachment requires a nonempty name. It renders the filename, optional human-readable size and status text, a decorative file icon or thumbnail, and an optional removal button. Positional component() children reject instead of disappearing. The component does not upload, download, open previews or remove itself. The application owns file access and authorization.

Top-level native attributes and @events target HTMLDivElement. removeProps targets HTMLButtonElement; thumbnailProps targets HTMLImageElement. AttachmentProps, AttachmentRemoveProps, AttachmentThumbnailProps, AttachmentType and AttachmentStatusVariant are public. class merges with defaults; authored styles can override layout. The filename remains readable text and is repeated in a native title when visually truncated. Narrow layouts wrap size and status; logical flex direction follows inherited RTL. Include UI sources in Tailwind scanning and load the UI theme.

onRemove makes the removal button visible. It receives the native click event with an HTMLButtonElement currentTarget; read that target before awaiting. The name defaults to 'Remove ' plus the filename. Supply removeLabel to localize or clarify it. The button always uses type=button and does not submit a containing form. Native Enter/Space activate it. removeProps supports disabled, ?disabled, native event handlers, data attributes and aria-describedby; native disabled fieldsets also apply. Its action type, role and accessible name are component-owned. A removeProps @click handler runs before onRemove and can preventDefault to veto removal. preventDefault(handler) also vetoes it and retains the directive's novalidate option. Disabling the button inside the native callback suppresses onRemove. A root bubble listener runs after the button action and is too late to veto it.

Removal is a callback request. The owning list must update its records and move focus to the next or previous item, or a stable external control when the last item disappears. The component cannot know that destination. Native focus remains on the same button across ordinary property updates; no global listeners or timers are installed. Callback failures and asynchronous work remain caller-owned. Without JavaScript the card is readable; the callback action requires hydration.

status is plain localized text. statusVariant explicitly selects neutral (default), success or error colors; words such as 'upload failed' never choose colors. The badge has no automatic live region. If updates need announcements, use an application-owned persistent status region and avoid duplicate announcements. Color alone must not carry the status meaning; supply descriptive status text.

type explicitly selects file, image, audio, video, archive or code. Otherwise a known final filename extension is matched case-insensitively. Extensionless, dot-only hidden names and unknown extensions use file. Icons are decorative. thumbnail replaces the icon with a native decorative img: src comes from thumbnail, alt is empty and aria-hidden is true because the filename already identifies the file. thumbnailProps supports loading, decoding, referrerpolicy and native image events, but cannot replace the source/alternative or add a focus stop. A broken image keeps the filename and card; no fallback/retry lifecycle or synthetic load/error callbacks are supplied. Browser networking and image caching remain native.

SSR, published type tests, themed Chromium hydration, real native keyboard/events, form and disabled-fieldset checks, localized status/names, image load/error events, narrow/RTL geometry and source-ejection compilation cover this foundation. The parent-removal fixture explicitly owns focus recovery. Other engines, assistive technologies, generated-app/runtime acceptance and the complete release matrix remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Bubble, Message and Marker display contracts
guides.summary: Compose typed chat rows with native child actions, readable reaction labels, explicit timestamps and responsive RTL layout.
guides.markdown:
Bubble, Message and Marker forward top-level native attributes and @events to their HTMLDivElement root. Their closed public prop types replace ignored arbitrary properties. They add no button role, Tab stop, keyboard shortcuts, live announcements or application actions. Child links, buttons, inputs and other renderer content retain native behavior. Use explicit type=button for child actions inside forms. Root event currentTarget is the div, even when the event originated in a child. Supply document/list semantics at the owning transcript; visual chat rows do not imply a log or accessibility compliance.

Bubble supports sent/received and default/pill/square variants. Invalid values reject. Its full-width root aligns an intrinsic-width content box at the logical start or end. The content box has a default maximum of 75% of the available width, with long-word wrapping. The CSS custom property --cs-bubble-max-width can change that limit. Sent/received corners and reaction alignment use logical edges, including RTL. Authored CSS and oversized child media remain caller-owned. Keep scrollable code/table content inside appropriately constrained native containers.

Bubble reactions is a readonly array of BubbleReaction records. Each record requires nonempty emoji and label strings; label is a localized text equivalent such as Like or Celebrate. The emoji is decorative, and label is exposed as screen-reader text. Optional count must be a nonnegative safe integer; zero is visible and undefined omits the count. The named native list defaults to reactionsLabel:Reactions; localize it as needed. These are display-only list items, not toggles or buttons. Interactive reaction controls belong in child content with application-owned state. Reactions wrap in normal flow below the content, reserving room before timestamps and later messages. They do not announce automatically. Updating records requires the parent to rerender.

Bubble and Message accept time as display text. Without datetime, arbitrary strings such as Just now remain ordinary span text. With an explicit nonempty datetime and nonempty time, a native time element carries that machine-readable value. The caller must supply a valid HTML timestamp and owns time zones, formatting and locale; the component does not parse or convert it. Put the timestamp on either Message or Bubble to avoid unnecessary duplication.

Message preserves supplied name, time and avatar for both sent and received rows. Omit any metadata you do not want displayed; sent no longer silently drops it. The optional avatar slot owns its alternative text and any native action. The body uses up to 80% of the available row, can shrink beside an avatar, and sets --cs-bubble-max-width:100% so nested bubbles do not acquire a second percentage limit. Sent rows place the avatar at the logical end; received rows place it at the start. Pass matching variants to Message and child Bubble because they are separate components. Names and metadata wrap at narrow widths. Name is readable text, not an automatically generated accessible group name.

Marker accepts default/unread styling and phrasing children such as Today, a time element, or inline text. Its two lines are decorative and hidden from accessibility; its label stays readable. unread changes color only and does not report new messages or move focus. It adds no separator role or splitter interaction. Localize children in the application.

SSR, published types, themed Chromium hydration, accessibility-tree text for reaction labels, native event targets, Tab/Enter/Space/link behavior, draft focus/value preservation during changes, timestamps, wrapped reactions, narrow/RTL geometry and strict source ejection cover these foundations. The generated Chat render fixture uses its real template and UI with supplied records/callbacks; it does not prove transport/server behavior. Load the UI theme and include component sources in Tailwind scanning. Other engines, assistive technologies, MessageScroller, blocks/icons and generated-app/runtime release gates remain separate. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: MessageScroller viewport, following and reading anchors
guides.summary: Own native transcript scrolling, user reading position, latest-message focus and observer/frame cleanup.
guides.markdown:
MessageScroller requires a stable document-unique id and a nonempty label for its viewport. Native top-level attributes/@events target the outer HTMLDivElement. viewportProps targets the actual scrolling HTMLDivElement; jumpProps targets the native HTMLButtonElement. MessageScrollerProps, MessageScrollerViewportProps and MessageScrollerJumpProps are public. The component owns the root/viewport identity, named region role, viewport tabindex:0, jump action type/name and aria-controls. The viewport ID is id-viewport. Apply an explicit height through root style or a height-constrained parent; the default height is 100%. Read event.currentTarget.scrollTop synchronously from viewportProps @scroll, not from a separate outer div. Caller native handlers run before internal updates. Cancelable key or jump events can be vetoed with preventDefault, including the renderer directive. Ordinary scroll events are not cancelable.

initialPosition is start or end (default end), captured when mounted. Existing browser focus within the viewport or a nonzero scroll offset takes precedence over initial following. Server HTML is a named, keyboard-scrollable region with normal child controls. Enhanced following and the jump button require hydration. Pre-hydration input values, focus and reading position remain browser-owned. threshold is a finite, nonnegative number of CSS pixels (default 80). Native scrolling into that distance from the bottom resumes following. Upward wheel/viewport keyboard input pauses following; keys inside child controls retain native behavior.

When following, appended records, streaming text, media dimensions and viewport resizing keep the bottom visible. Focusing a child control pauses automatic following so arriving content does not move an editor out of view. While reading history, the component remembers visible direct element children and their top offsets. On content/size changes it preserves the first surviving visible element. If that element disappears, a surviving visible sibling supplies the anchor; if none survives, the previous numeric scroll offset is clamped by the browser. Use stable keyed child elements (for example repeat with stable message IDs) so prepends/reorders retain DOM identity. Text-only children, rebuilt nodes and edits inside one long row do not provide word-level anchors. Browser scroll anchoring is disabled to avoid competing adjustments. Author overrides to geometry or anchoring own their effects.

ResizeObservers watch the viewport, content and direct rows; a MutationObserver catches structural, text and relevant style changes. Geometry changes that clamp scrollTop do not count as a user choosing to follow. Pointer, wheel, focus and viewport key intent refresh the reading snapshot before native movement. Work is coalesced into an owned animation frame. Ref setup is deferred until the nodes connect, guarded by component lifetime. Cleanup disconnects both observers, drops retained row references, cancels pending frames and prevents queued setup from reattaching.

jumpLabel defaults to Scroll to latest messages and can be localized. The button appears when the viewport is farther than threshold from the bottom; it does not assert that unread messages exist. It is a native non-submit button with keyboard activation and disabled support through jumpProps. Its click can be vetoed by a native caller handler. When the focused button disappears, focus returns to the viewport without scrolling. Removing, hiding or disabling a focused message control repairs focus to the viewport; keyed updates retain eligible focus without overwriting the reading anchor.

The public browser method scrollToBottom() immediately follows the latest content. It uses instant scrolling, including under reduced-motion preferences. If an explicitly requested jump leaves a focused child outside the visible area, focus moves to the viewport. Valid calls while disconnected and server-side client-method calls are harmless. The old scrollRef and misleading newMessageLabel prop are removed. Initial-position changes after mount do not reset the user. Callback failures and external application work remain caller-owned.

The component adds no live region or unread counter. The generated Chat example names its transcript, exposes aria-busy while streaming and uses a separate short status announcement; it no longer wraps every streaming token in a transcript-wide live region. Applications own announcement policy, authentication and message loading. Source row anchoring is not virtualization or a persistence mechanism.

SSR and published types, themed Chromium with real native scroll/focus, no-JavaScript keyboard access, pre-hydration editing, append/stream/prepend/resize/late-image behavior, anchor removal/replacement, shrink/repopulate behavior, jump veto/disabled states and cleanup/remount checks cover this foundation. Observer accounting tracks component targets separately from Playwright's document observer. The framework demo and actual generated Chat render fixture cover integration at their stated scope. Source ejection and installed CLI/MCP guidance are checked separately. Other browser engines, assistive technologies, blocks/icons and the full generated-app/runtime matrix remain release gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Native SVG Icon
guides.summary: Compose trusted Solar artwork with typed native SVG attributes, events and accessible naming.
guides.markdown:
Import Icon and IconProps from @cossackframework/ui, and import individual entries such as ArrowRightIcon from @cossackframework/solar-icons/arrow-right. Use component(Icon, {entry: ArrowRightIcon, variant: 'bold', size: 24}). entry contains explicitly trusted SVG markup. It is not sanitized; never use untrusted user SVG as artwork.

variant selects line (default), bold, duotone, broken, outline or line-duotone. Missing variants fall back to the entry's own line artwork. Empty or unavailable artwork rejects. normalizeStyle converts supported legacy aliases to canonical variants and rejects unknown names. The old artwork style prop is now variant; style is native CSS. size must be positive and finite and owns both dimensions and the 24-unit viewBox.

Omit label or pass blank text for decoration. A nonempty label supplies role=img, aria-label and an SVG title. Icon owns naming and focus geometry; label text is escaped. Put interactive icons inside named native buttons or links, keeping keyboard actions and focus on those controls. Icon itself is not an interactive button.

Native SVG attributes, data-* values, class, style, fill, stroke and @event listeners bind to the SVG element. Event currentTarget is SVGSVGElement; target can be an artwork descendant. Capture currentTarget before awaiting. class merges with cs-icon. Positional children are rejected. Only artwork is raw; native attribute values and labels use normal renderer escaping. SVG creation and raw artwork updates preserve namespaces, including HTML inside foreignObject. This guide adds no executable example; broader runtime and accessibility acceptance remain separate gates.

guides.title: AuthForm credential and provider UI
guides.summary: Compose a named native authentication form with explicit provider callbacks, browser-owned credentials and cancellable UI work.
guides.markdown:
Import AuthForm, AuthFormProps, AuthFormData, AuthFormResult, AuthFormContext, AuthFormProvider, AuthFormLabels and AuthFormNativeProps from @cossackframework/ui/blocks. Blocks remain opt-in. Pass a stable page-unique id and an onSubmit callback. Native attributes and events on the root target HTMLDivElement; formProps targets HTMLFormElement. The block owns form identity, naming, submission method and validation. cossack add ui auth-form ejects this block using public primitive/type imports.

Choose defaultMode for local state (captured once, default login), or mode plus onModeChange for parent ownership. Do not combine mode and defaultMode. Controlled toggle clicks only propose a change. Both modes render correctly on the server. Name, email and password labels use IDs derived from the block ID. There are no shared hardcoded IDs. All visible text, including error fallback, pending state, mode actions and password reveal names, can be localized through labels. Browser-native validation messages follow browser locale.

The block reads FormData from the native form when submitting. It does not store credential values in reactive fields. PasswordInput omits a value binding when no value is supplied, preserving native edits and autofill. Hydration and reveal do not erase those values. Inputs are named and have appropriate autocomplete values. Login requires email and password but imposes no new password length policy. Signup defaults to eight characters; signupPasswordMinLength changes that constraint. Existing values are checked explicitly when the mode changes because adding native minlength does not always invalidate a previously entered value. Applications must still validate and authorize on the server.

Submission, provider and mode actions stay disabled until hydration, with an explanatory notice; native fields remain editable. The native form uses POST, never GET. This callback-based block does not supply a no-JavaScript authentication endpoint. Use an application-owned native form when progressive server POST authentication is required. Native email/required validation runs before credential submission. formProps @submit can veto with preventDefault; even a throwing listener cannot trigger default credential navigation.

onSubmit receives a discriminated AuthFormData record (login has email/password; signup also has name) and a context with AbortSignal. Callback return values are void or AuthFormResult containing safe localized error and fieldErrors text. Raw thrown exception messages are replaced with labels.failure. Empty success results only release pending UI; they do not assert authentication succeeded. The application owns session creation, redirects, password policy, server validation and authentication. Field errors have aria-invalid and matching descriptions; errors focus the first affected field only when focus has not moved outside. Editing a field clears its error and the general error.

providers is an explicit readonly list of unique IDs and visible labels. Supplying providers requires onSocial. Its callback receives the selected provider ID and context, never fabricated empty credentials. Provider buttons are keyed native non-submit actions and can run independently of credential validity. No Google, GitHub or OAuth flow is implicitly enabled.

Only one credential or provider request runs at a time. Controls and mode actions disable while pending; duplicate submit events are ignored. Mode changes from the parent and onCleanup abort the owned signal and invalidate late results. Callback failures remain observed. Cancellation is cooperative: it cannot stop ignored I/O or undo authentication side effects. No request is automatically replayed. Input values remain in the current DOM until the application clears or unmounts the form.

SSR, public type failures, themed Chromium for published and ejected implementations, pre-hydration input, native keyboard/validation, reveal, provider actions, field errors, focus, disabled state, cancellation and remounts cover this foundation. Existing PasswordInput browser regressions remain relevant. Other browser engines, assistive technologies and real backend/session acceptance remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Composed CommandPalette
guides.summary: Build a grouped command launcher with native dialog ownership, explicit shortcuts, stable selection and optional icon/hint presentation.
guides.markdown:
Import CommandPalette, CommandPaletteProps and CommandItem from @cossackframework/ui/blocks. This opt-in block composes the public Command primitive. It owns no second Modal, search controller or global shortcut listener. Supply a stable page-unique id, nonempty dialog label, readonly commands and onSelect(id). Native attributes, class, style and @events target HTMLDialogElement. The outer cs-command-palette div is only a composition marker. Positional children are unsupported. cossack add ui command-palette ejects the source using public UI imports.

Commands require unique nonempty IDs and nonempty labels. group creates named visual groups, ordered by each first matching group. Keyboard navigation follows the same displayed order, including after filtering or regrouping. disabled commands remain visible but cannot be selected. icon is explicitly trusted SVG artwork; use a direct Solar entry import. shortcut is a display hint, not a key binding. description supplies accessible supporting text and defaults to the shortcut hint. Icons and visible keyboard hints do not replace the option name.

Use defaultOpen for local state, captured once. Use open plus onOpenChange for parent ownership; do not combine open and defaultOpen. setOpen(boolean) and toggle() propose state changes. Controlled parents must accept proposals through props. Rejected native dismissals reopen the dialog. Prop-driven changes and cleanup do not create dismissal proposals. The block keeps local state separate from mirrored props.

SSR renders one closed native dialog with stable search/result relationships. It opens modally on client connection when requested, focuses the named search field, traps native modal focus and restores the opener on dismissal. Localize label, searchLabel, placeholder, emptyLabel and closeLabel. Escape, close and backdrop behavior use the same controller as Command. Native @cancel can veto Escape. Search resets on accepted open-state changes.

Search trims surrounding whitespace and matches labels case-insensitively. Focus remains in the combobox; aria-activedescendant identifies the active option. Arrow keys wrap through enabled matches and Enter selects. Composition and modified editing keys keep native behavior. Empty or all-disabled results have no active descendant. Stable IDs preserve highlight through updates; removing the active command chooses the first enabled match. onSelect is called before the closing proposal. Action return values and promises are not awaited; applications own action errors, routing and authorization. A thrown synchronous callback leaves the palette open.

shortcut=true explicitly enables Ctrl/Meta+K; the default is false. Do not register a competing application listener. Command arbitrates all connected owners in document order and restricts handling to an existing active modal. Closed owners ignore editable controls unless shortcutInEditable=true; an open palette can toggle from its own search field. Prevented, repeating, composing, Alt and Shift events are ignored. Use a single app-level shortcut owner and explicit triggers for local palettes. Cleanup delegates to Command and removes its listener/registration and closes the dialog.

Published and ejected implementations pass themed HTTP Chromium checks for grouping, icons/hints, native names, keyboard/pointer behavior, controlled rejection, editor shortcuts, multiple owners, foreign modals, imperative methods, focus restoration and listener cleanup. The framework block demo and shell navigation also pass real application checks. Studio uses explicit identity, naming and trigger attributes. Other engines, assistive technologies and full runtime acceptance remain separate gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Native DashboardStat metrics
guides.summary: Display readonly metrics with stable identities, native list semantics and explicit change meaning.
guides.markdown:
Import DashboardStat, DashboardStatProps, StatItem, StatTrend and StatTone from @cossackframework/ui/blocks. Supply a readonly stats array. Each metric needs a stable nonempty id unique within the list, a nonempty label and a finite number or nonempty preformatted string value. Zero is preserved. Formatting, units, comparison periods and data loading belong to the caller. Duplicate IDs and invalid values throw. Stable IDs preserve list-item identity through updates and reordering; do not use array positions for identity.

The root is a native ul with role=list. Native attributes, class, style and @events target HTMLUListElement. Give the list a useful accessible name such as aria-label='Overview metrics'. Each item contains native dt/dd label/value definitions. Positional children are unsupported. Optional icon entries are explicitly trusted decorative SVG artwork; import Solar entries directly. Icons do not replace metric text.

change is optional localized text. trend and tone require change. trend is up, down or neutral and describes direction only. tone is positive, negative or neutral and defaults to neutral independently of direction. A rising cost can have trend='up' and tone='negative'; fewer errors can have trend='down' and tone='positive'. Direction has visible Increase/Decrease/No change text. Positive/negative meaning has visible Favorable/Unfavorable text as well as color. Customize trendLabels and toneLabels for localization; defined labels must be nonempty. Neutral tone makes no assessment. Omit trend when direction is unknown rather than asserting no change.

columns accepts 2, 3 or 4 and defaults to 4. The grid has one column on narrow screens, two from sm, then the selected count from md. Long labels and values wrap. Empty arrays render an empty list. The block does not fetch, sort, announce live updates or provide row actions. Applications own data freshness, loading/errors, authorization and announcements where needed.

cossack add ui dashboard-stat ejects source with public UI imports. Public types, SSR and themed HTTP Chromium tests cover published/ejected implementations, zero, invalid metrics, native events, SVG artwork, explicit tones, narrow layouts and keyed updates. Full runtime and assistive-technology acceptance remain separate release gates. This guide adds no executable example.

guides.title: Native SettingsPanel ownership
guides.summary: Compose labeled settings controls with explicit controlled/default values, native reset and safe action buttons.
guides.markdown:
Import SettingsPanel, SettingsPanelProps, SettingsSection, SettingsRow and SettingsValues from @cossackframework/ui/blocks. Supply a stable page-unique id and readonly sections. Sections require unique nonempty id/title and readonly rows. Every row needs a nonempty label and a stable key unique across the panel. Keys own control identity and default native names. Changing a key changes identity. Text rows use string values; switch rows use booleans. Missing values default to empty text or false. Invalid schema and value types throw. A row is a discriminated union: text rows accept placeholder, autocomplete, readonly and required; switches accept required; both accept optional native name. All rows accept disabled, hint and badge. Button rows require action text and use explicit outline or destructive variant; keys such as delete have no special visual behavior. Button rows require the panel onAction callback.

Use values plus onChange for controlled state. The parent accepts a proposed snapshot through new props. Rejected changes restore the actual native input, even when the accepted value has not changed. Otherwise use defaultValues, captured once, with optional onChange. Local edits remain independent of later defaultValues changes. Do not combine values/defaultValues or change ownership after the first render. SettingsValues and supplied records are readonly. onChange receives a fresh complete snapshot for current text/switch rows; mutating that snapshot does not mutate local state. Extra values are not rendered or emitted. Local keyed values survive temporary row removal; newly added rows use their captured default or empty/false. Reusing a key with a different control type can fail validation: use a new key for a different control.

The root is a typed HTMLDivElement with class, style, native attributes and @events. Each section is named by its heading. Text controls have connected labels; switches have native checkbox/switch semantics and labels; hints are connected through aria-describedby. Names default to keys but may be supplied explicitly. Buttons are always type=button, with action text as their name and row label/hint as descriptions. They neither submit nor reset the surrounding form. Panel disabled and row disabled use native disabled state. Readonly text stays focusable and submits normally. The block owns its root tabindex=-1 as a focus fallback and accepts no positional children.

The block does not create a form. Place it inside an application-owned form for native submission and reset. Unchecked switches follow native FormData behavior and are absent. Required fields participate in native validation when the form is submitted. A successful native reset proposes the initial value snapshot captured on first render. Local state accepts it; controlled parents may accept or reject it. Preventing the reset event prevents the proposal. Each reset settles after the native default action; cleanup cancels pending callbacks. Listener setup handles SSR hydration and fresh client rendering. Resetting a containing form resets disabled fields too, as native reset does.

Stable keyed rows retain controls during updates. Focus repair runs after nested rendering: it restores the same enabled control after movement, chooses an available control after removal/disable, or focuses the root when none remain. It does not steal focus from another active control. Text values use reactive DOM properties, not stale value attributes. The layout stacks controls on narrow screens. Native fields are initialized from the supplied values during hydration; use application state as the initial source of truth.

onChange and onAction are synchronous notifications. Their return values and promises are not awaited; applications own asynchronous errors, persistence, authorization and confirmation. A thrown onChange still restores controlled DOM state. The block supplies no save request, server validation or action retry. cossack add ui settings-panel ejects source using public imports. SSR, public types and themed HTTP Chromium cover published/ejected implementations, hydration/fresh rendering, controlled rejection, reset/veto, callback failures, row focus and cleanup. Other engines, assistive technologies and the full runtime matrix remain release gates. This guide adds no executable example.
